title: Convert Volley to a Go executable with durable review state
description:
Volley is a planner/critic specification-review engine. Today it is a Bash script (`volley.sh`) with two thin role launchers (`cc-volley`, `codex-volley`). It drives two agent CLIs (Claude and Codex) through a draft, critique, revise loop, either directly or through Gashki (a tmux pane controller).

Problems with the Bash engine that this epic fixes:
- Round and recovery state is inferred from file counts and modification times, so a crash can lose or repeat work.
- A requested CLI timeout can be silently ignored when `timeout` is not installed.
- Verdict detection can match a substring anywhere; a missing verdict becomes an implicit REVISE.
- A lost or malformed send to a Gashki pane has incomplete cursor evidence, so recovery can paste a prompt twice.
- Settings come from environment variables and ambient vendor defaults, so a rerun can pick different models.
- Output modes and exit codes are not a complete machine contract.
- The planner agent can write any workspace file, including state and binding inputs.

Goal: replace the Bash engine with one Go executable that separates command parsing, settings, review transitions, saved state, agent calls, prompts, and user answers. The tool records resolved settings before it starts any agent. A later process can inspect and resume the same run from explicit saved state without guessing the phase from files. A run finishes only after the artifact and required review steps meet declared completion rules.

Main workflow: the user starts a review from a brief or an existing specification, chooses roles, models, effort, a backend and a round budget. Agents draft, critique and revise inside the workspace. When a user decision is needed, the tool records a question and stops requesting new loop turns. The user can answer through a command, a workspace file, the controller terminal, or the Gashki planner pane.

End-to-end success test (the epic is not done until this passes with stub agents, on both backends, with planner/critic roles swapped):
1. Start a review with a TOML settings file and a small brief.
2. Observe a revision and a question through stub agents.
3. Interrupt the controller after a confirmed send and before the result is recorded.
4. Resume from saved state without submitting that prompt again.
5. Apply one user answer to both roles exactly once in the logical review sequence.
6. Finish with a final artifact, checked review evidence, settings records and a complete run record.
7. Repeat the settings in a fresh workspace after changing ambient defaults.
8. Obtain the same tool-controlled settings and argument choices.
9. Perform these checks through both backends with roles reversed.
This does not claim identical model output. It does not claim a saved settings file reproduces authentication, vendor defaults, source contents or a model service.
design:
Source baseline: repository commit `a7252e474023f986d9912469b1e58742e644afc8` (Bash engine plus prompts and four critic rubric fragments). The Bash test matrix recorded 588 passing assertions; that is historical evidence, not a target number for the Go tests. Gashki was inspected at commit `8eaecc9b31c965bab6c63a6a5562ebf38c43e363` (contract version 2, Go 1.26.1). The Go 1.26.1 toolchain must be confirmed on the build machine (first task).

Module `github.com/TheEditor/volley`, Go 1.26.1. Package layout:
- `cmd/volley/main.go` thin entry point
- `internal/{cli,config,contract,review,store,process,gashki,agent,prompt,human,conformance}`
- `prompts/` embedded Markdown templates; `tests/scenarios`, `tests/stubs`; `testdata/golden`, `testdata/migration`; `scripts/`
Dependencies: go-toml/v2 v2.4.3 (with its unstable ranges adapter for edit-preserving writes), santhosh-tekuri/jsonschema/v6 v6.0.3, golang.org/x/sys v0.48.0, standard library for the rest. No jq, yq, Python or PTY dependency in the engine. Platforms: macOS and Linux first; reject any other process-control platform before an agent call.

User requirements (U01-U15, binding):
- U01 Convert Volley to Go; one final engine.
- U02 Choose code structure before implementing configuration reform.
- U03 Similar structure and command rules across Volley, Gashki and rr-run.
- U04 Each tool owns its own TOML file and settings.
- U05 Settings resolve flag > file > default. Retire the tool's own setting environment variables.
- U06 Keep the default XDG configuration path. A missing named file is an error.
- U07 Use an off-the-shelf TOML library. Preserve types in reusable setting records.
- U08 Save resolved settings for Volley and Gashki before dependent execution.
- U09 L0 owns identity and credentials; L1 owns the job and agent choices; L2 owns execution mechanisms.
- U10 Keep explicit user requirements and binding constraints in the review.
- U11 Agents resolve technical objections together when evidence permits.
- U12 Future execution approvals remain gates. Reviewing this plan grants no execution permission.
- U13 One integrated specification with dependency-aware tasks and acceptance cases.
- U14 Planning documents stay outside the repository; one Volley handoff.
- U15 Report to the user in ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English.

Design decisions (P01-P17):
- P01 Keep both backends (direct CLI and Gashki).
- P02 Keep workspace artifacts; `state/manifest.json` is the authoritative checkpoint.
- P03 Derived XDG run index for discovery only; never an execution authority.
- P04 Run creation is foreground-only; no background service.
- P05 Local OS locks for controller ownership and short file-edit transactions; a crashed process must not keep ownership via a timer.
- P06 Native commands return at a question unless `--wait` is given.
- P07 Legacy launchers keep waiting behavior; their exit-code mapping is documented separately.
- P08 Final-line verdict grammar; missing verdict retried once then recorded as MISSING, never approval.
- P09 Run the enabled closing pass once after first approval when a confirmation round remains; remove keyword-based remark detection.
- P10 Review any changed closing artifact again before final approval.
- P11 A new user directive gets a planner application turn before the next critic turn; both roles then see the same directive.
- P12 Keep the advisory second opinion; once per run in a fresh session.
- P13 No premise-review stage, distillation stage, multiple critics, or build stage.
- P14 Keep vendor adapters local; do not import another tool's internal packages or add a shared framework.
- P15 Explicit handover for uncertain delivery; recovery never creates an automatic duplicate prompt.
- P16 Keep legacy evidence; supply detection, a read-only legacy report and a fresh-workspace recipe; defer native import and legacy session reuse.
- P17 macOS and Linux first.

Command standard: follow the make-cli standard at revision `26f47a9a621862b63f3d7baccbb2ca7e441f5254` (archetype: build/task orchestrator with a state inspection surface; canonical task: plan, execute, inspect and resume one specification review). Departures from that standard, to be recorded in capabilities output, the guide and the changelog:
- D01 No setting environment precedence and no settings profiles.
- D02 Foreground creation instead of detached job submission.
- D03 Local OS ownership locks instead of TTL reservations (a TTL can expire during a long agent turn; the OS lock ends with the owner but does not prove the agent stopped).
- D04 `runs` names the durable jobs; no parallel `jobs` aliases.
- D05 Delivery supports stdout, file and null only; no webhook sink.
- D06 Boolean setting flags take one `true` or `false` value; selectors take no value. Gashki's `--here` and `--trust-folder` have arity 0 but Volley's `--trust-folder` has arity 1; the guide must show `volley ... --trust-folder=true` and explain this.

Explicit behavior changes from the Bash engine (C01-C15). Each has acceptance cases in the child tasks and must be documented in the guide before the Go executable becomes the default:
- C01 Explicit phase, round, turn intent, receipt and artifact hashes replace file-count inference.
- C02 Answers bind to question generations and recorded file observations, not modification times.
- C03 Turn duration is enforced by the Go process runner (no dependence on `timeout`/`gtimeout`).
- C04 Exactly one final non-empty verdict line is accepted.
- C05 Missing verdict after retry is recorded as MISSING; revision requested conservatively; never claimed as a received REVISE.
- C06 The enabled closing pass reads the approval and advisory reviews when a confirmation round remains; otherwise notes and the skip reason are saved.
- C07 If the closing pass changes the artifact hash, another critic round is required.
- C08 A user directive is applied through the planner before the next critique.
- C09 A lost send recovers through a checked same-key Gashki call; malformed or unverifiable evidence hands over; never substitute an unqualified idle wait.
- C10 Intended persistent identity is saved before launch; observed identity as soon as received.
- C11 Explicit ownership and retention results per external action replace shared cleanup flags.
- C12 Tool settings are frozen; unknown vendor choices are recorded as unknown.
- C13 Versioned envelope, registry, schemas and conformance surface.
- C14 Billing/auth guard checks effective direct roots and the checked Gashki execution identity context.
- C15 Direct Claude planner uses `dontAsk`, declared Skill availability and role-specific path rules; state, frozen configs, binding inputs and committed history are protected; a planner change stops with PLANNER_MUTATION; controller artifact names are reserved. Vendor enforcement stays unverified until the live gate.

Exclusions: no Rally dispatch, Agentty integration, Ollama, batch reviews, tournaments, generic adapter registry, implementation of an approved spec, build-stage agents, changes to Gashki source or hook contract, rr-run implementation, settings profiles, remote state storage, daemon, webhook delivery, automatic credential management. The existing open issues about pluggable agents, schema-enforced verdicts, telemetry, dual-run comparison and a maintainer briefing document are separate and are not part of this epic; overlap with structured verdicts or telemetry is limited to the requirements written here.

Gates that no task may bypass:
- Build-order gate: the planned build order is Gashki setting reform, Gashki parser replacement, rr-run, then Volley. Gashki setting reform is complete in the examined source. Gashki parser replacement and the reviewed rr-run build are not established as complete. Drafting and isolated proof work may proceed. Before product implementation starts, confirm those predecessor results or record a user-approved order change.
- Live vendor launches (tier C, at most 8 new conversation launches) need separate explicit user approval after the procedure is concrete. No approval is inherited from another project.
- Release publication needs its own authorization. Reviewing this plan and settling its technical points grant no execution permission.
- A not-run case is not a pass. A stub pass is never reported as a live vendor pass.

Child tasks are T01..T25 (task IDs referenced inside each issue). Checkpoints: K1 contracts and proofs (T01-T10); K2 direct loop plus separate Gashki adapter checks (T11-T16); K3 complete integrated behavior (T17-T22); K4 default switch and release readiness (T23-T25). Dependency edges between children are authoritative and acyclic. First runnable review slice is T16 (direct stubs, ordinary approval, auxiliary passes disabled); T22 adds the Gashki adapter and pane-answer settlement to the same loop.

title: T10 Implement prompts, rubric delivery, and role instructions
description: Why: the Bash engine builds prompts by string concatenation in the shell, which makes exact user text, role-specific rules and rubric delivery hard to prove. The review agents only behave consistently if every role prompt carries the same common review rule exactly once, only critics see the rubric, and exact human directive text survives rendering. The Go engine needs a small typed literal renderer over embedded Markdown templates, with template hashes and rendered-prompt hashes recorded for every turn, so a prompt can never silently change or contain an unresolved placeholder.
design:
Work: embed the shipped Markdown templates into the executable and add typed literal rendering for all turn purposes, directive blocks, backend answer instructions, and the exact common review rule. Keep template hashes separate from rendered prompt hashes. Do not ask planners for separate response files; the tool captures the final reply.

1. Template source. Keep the short current prompt shape and external Markdown source files in the repository (readable for maintenance): `prompts/planner-init.md`, `prompts/planner-revise.md`, `prompts/critic.md`, `prompts/closing-pass.md` and `prompts/profiles/{security,data,decision-memo,plan-spec}.md`. The current templates use `{{ROUND}}`, `{{HUMAN}}`, `{{CONTEXT}}`, `{{CONSTRAINTS}}`, `{{SECOND_OPINION}}` markers. Embed shipped prompts and rubric fragments into the Go executable for installed use. There is no arbitrary prompt-directory setting in this build; any future override needs its own versioning and resume rules.
2. Renderer. Literal placeholder substitution through a small typed renderer. Reject unknown or unresolved placeholders before any mutation or delivery. Substituted user text is never re-scanned (no recursive substitution): a user directive that contains marker-like text such as a placeholder survives byte for byte. Record template hash and rendered hash for every turn; they differ correctly.
3. Common review rule. Append the common review rule exactly once to ALL prompt purposes: draft, revision, directive application, critique, reminder, advisory review, closing, confirmation. Content of the rule (retained from the Bash baseline commit `a7252e4`): agents resolve technical design objections together; they ask the user only when an explicit user requirement must change or when evidence cannot settle a user preference; a critic's demand for a user answer is not itself binding; proposed choices remain proposals until approved for execution through the relevant process.
4. Question format instructions. Only the planner writes open questions: it numbers each, supplies options and a recommendation, and uses the recommendation provisionally in SPEC.md. When none remain, QUESTIONS.md is absent or empty (whitespace-only counts as empty; headings and answered-question records are not empty). Decided facts stay in the spec; history stays in archived inputs. Add backend-specific question/answer instructions to planner prompts only (with Gashki the planner also lists questions at the end of its visible reply).
5. Directives. Bind human directives after their archived question and preserve original answer text (no trimming or summarizing; keep line breaks). An application turn prompt includes the exact archived question and answer where applicable; the critic sees the same archived directive in that round.
6. Rubric. Only critic prompts receive the selected rubric fragment (empty, security, data, decision-memo, plan-spec). The advisory (second-opinion) critic gets the same rubric plus an explicit advisory-scope statement. Planner prompts never receive the rubric.
7. Verdict reminder prompt: refers to the missing final line, preserves the common review rule and binding inputs, and uses a new logical attempt ID without overwriting the first reply (the exact verdict grammar is `VERDICT: APPROVE` / `VERDICT: REVISE` as the final non-empty line).
8. Skills. Claude skill access uses its effective skills folder plus resolved read-only symlink targets. Record the referenced root list without copying contents. Use supported read permission rules and one system instruction naming the skills path. Do not grant write access to skill roots or to the reference context. Codex reads the effective CODEX_HOME skill setup through its existing environment; a scratch CODEX_HOME needs its own required skill links, and the user's config.toml must not be copied. Missing optional skills are reported when a brief requires them, before claiming the standard was applied.

Outputs: prompt package and captured-prompt fixtures for both providers, both backends, and all turn purposes.

Fixtures used: F-PURE (owned temp workspace, fake clock, fixed IDs, pure interfaces, no agents).

Done when: every prompt has the common rule once; critic prompts alone receive the rubric; exact user text survives directive rendering; unresolved placeholders fail before delivery.
- A-PROMPT-01 (tier A, F-PURE): renderer harness supplies role/backend metadata for draft, revision, reminder, directive, ordinary/advisory critique, closing, and confirmation with constraints/context. Required: the common rule appears once in every purpose. Exact directives survive. Rubric only reaches critic purposes. Template/rendered hashes differ correctly. No provider adapter is required. Covers U10-U12, C08.
- A-PROMPT-02 (tier A, F-PURE): literal placeholder-like user text, unknown template marker, linked skills, missing required skill. Required: user text is not recursively substituted. An unresolved template marker refuses before delivery. Skill read roots are recorded with no write rule and no copied private config. Covers C13, C15, U10.
- Evidence rules for every case: report ID, tier, fixture, stimulus variant, source/binary hashes, settings, target OS, observed output, artifact hashes. A plan, a source comment, or a stub that merely returns the required answer is not evidence.

Embedded source, bundle, and rendered hashes are separate. Skill planning records resolved linked read roots, refuses missing required skills, uses Read rules only, and creates required scratch Codex links without copying configuration. Captured fixture covers 180 provider/backend/purpose/rubric combinations. A-PROMPT-01 and A-PROMPT-02 pass on macOS and Linux; full Go suite, prompt race checks, vet, and diff checks pass. Evidence includes source/binary/artifact hashes and target settings. No vendor conversation ran. Implementation is ready to commit; adapter enforcement and live behavior remain later gates.

title: T11 Implement direct Claude and Codex adapters
description: Why: the default backend runs the Claude and Codex command-line tools directly, one process per turn. The Bash engine builds those argument lists and parses their output inline in the main script, so session identity, permissions and partial output are fragile (C10, C15). The Go engine needs a small direct backend per provider that builds exact argument arrays, writes one permissions settings object for Claude, parses Codex structured events to capture its thread ID immediately, never invents a replacement session, and keeps all outputs in owned files. It must not contain a round loop: it supplies primitive operations that the review-engine task later wraps with the protected-set comparator.
design:
Work: build provider argument arrays, one Claude settings object, tool restrictions, owned outputs, and Codex structured event/session parsing. Save the Claude intended session UUID before launch and the Codex observed thread ID immediately on its valid event. Handle a failed resume without creating a replacement session. Supply primitive direct operations to the declared GuardedTurnExecutor interface; call the frozen-config hash gate from the records task before each launch; register exact output sinks for the protected-set comparator from the state task. Unit tests use an executor spy; the review-engine task owns the real pre/post guard wiring. Share the process runner and storage code; no round loop here.

1. Typed turn interface. Define `TurnRequest`, `PreparedTurn`, `DeliveryReceipt`, `CompletionReceipt`, `TurnOutcome`, `RetentionDecision`. A request binds run ID, turn ID, purpose, role, round, prompt bytes/hash, expected artifact paths, spec-before hash and session identity. A preparation result includes proposed argv or send payload, capability facts and intended identity. A completion result includes observed status, reply result, artifact facts, observed identity and evidence references. Outcome kinds: completed, definitely-not-started, delivery-uncertain, running-with-cursor, failed-with-evidence, identity-conflict. Cleanup is separate from turn success. A reply result is found, pending, unsupported-format, missing or read-failed. A missing/pending reply can warn after its bounded capture interval; a missing required artifact cannot.
2. Direct capability facts: process per turn; exact vendor resume ID required when persistent; completion evidence is process status plus vendor/output protocol; Codex direct critic supports an OS read-only sandbox; cancellation stops the owned agent through process-group policy; placement not applicable; no user answer in a planner pane; binary override is the active resolved CLI path. A capability declaration is not a security claim beyond its actual mechanism. Prompts and post-turn hashes are not an OS sandbox.
3. Arguments and output (all providers). Build all arguments as slices, no shell expansion or joined command execution. Set cwd to the workspace. Default stdin to the null device. Keep stdout, stderr, final reply and exit facts in owned files. Use a same-directory temporary output file and promote it only after validation. Preserve failed/partial output under the turn evidence directory.
4. Claude. Print mode, explicit model/effort when supplied, declared file tools, permission mode `dontAsk`. (This changes the old direct planner's acceptEdits mode and adds direct Skill availability: behavior change C15.) Generate one settings JSON object with `encoding/json`. Its `permissions.allow` array carries the role-specific rules. Its `permissions.deny` array forbids Edit/Write for the canonical reference context and checked skill roots. For each Claude planner (direct or Gashki) it also forbids writes to `state/**`, `volley.config.toml`, `gashki.config.toml`, `BRIEF.md` and `CONSTRAINTS.md`. Generate path-specific deny rules for every existing committed rounds artifact before each direct turn. New planner review-history files remain permitted under rounds. Use the vendor-supported Edit rule form that covers both Edit and Write (verify at the live gate). Do not assume a narrow allow rule cancels a broader inherited allow rule. Record the effective permission setup without secrets. If inherited permissions cannot meet the declared write boundary, fail preparation rather than widen the role. Include skill read rules and the `[1m]` model-suffix override in that same object rather than in competing settings flags. The direct critic's file-tool set is read-only and its reply is captured by Volley. The Skill allowance is declared and tested without claiming every skill dependency is available.

Role/backend table (apply to main and auxiliary turns; direct rows are this task, Gashki rows are in the Gashki tasks):

| Role and backend | Tool availability flag | Allow rules in the one settings object | Denial and output |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

Deadline and process rules come from the shared process runner (monotonic total turn budget; TERM, 5s grace, KILL; process-group ownership; never kill by PID alone; uncertain identity returns TURN_UNCERTAIN and requires inspection; no replacement turn from a partial spec; a next-turn action is released only after settlement and a valid recorded completion or explicit abandonment).

title: T12 Prepare and prove the pinned Gashki fixture
description: Why: the Gashki backend drives real tmux panes through a separate tool. Before any Volley adapter depends on Gashki behavior, the exact pinned release must be built, its contract subset checked, and a fully isolated fixture proven: its own tmux server, config, state roots, socket and owned stub vendor executables. Without that, tests could silently reach a real vendor binary, a user's real tmux server or the user's normal Gashki state. This is a mechanics proof with stubs: it does not prove live vendor behavior, which stays unverified until the separately approved live procedure.
design:
Work: create two verified Gashki artifacts from the pinned source (commit `8eaecc9b31c965bab6c63a6a5562ebf38c43e363`, contract version 2): a release-style build without the `gashkitest` tag, and a separate `gashkitest` build for named fault-seam cases. Save distinct binary hashes and build tags. Use the release-style artifact for all normal tier-B cases; use the test artifact only for named fault cases (including the send-barrier cases) and clear its triggers before the same-key recovery call. Do not assume an installed `gashki` binary matches the repository source; verify the binary used.

1. Preflight facts to check. Resolved Gashki binary version, capabilities and required schemas before dependent mutations. Require contract 2 and the checked subset for `config show/get`, `spawn`, `send`, `wait`, `observe`, `status`, `kill`. Required flags: `--agent`, `--cwd`, `--agent-args`, `--here`, `--trust-folder`, `--json`, `--from-stdin`, `--idempotency-key`, `--until`, `--since`, `--wait-timeout`, and `--yes` on kill. A version-text match alone is insufficient. Record the verified binary path/hash and the contract snapshot hash.
2. Release posture. Verify the release-style artifact has compiled-out injection: `GASHKI_TEST_FAULT` and `GASHKI_TEST_HOLD` cannot activate. The pinned source makes them inert (no failure injected, no hold), rather than returning a trigger-refusal error; verify that exact posture and do not require a new Gashki feature.
3. Isolation. Create a fresh named tmux server plus an explicit Gashki config, state root, XDG roots, TMPDIR and TMUX_TMPDIR. Unset inherited TMUX before preparing the server. Create owned `claude` and `codex` stub executables earlier on the isolated PATH. They implement the required startup screen and hooks without any vendor service call. The fixture must never fall back to a real vendor executable: prove the resolved provider path belongs to the fixture before spawn. Only remove panes, servers, roots and files the fixture created and recorded. Never run Gashki's full suite against the user's normal state roots.
4. Mechanism checks: startup, merged settings (hooks plus role rules), capabilities, required response fields, cursor timing, server identity (actual socket path from the matching `pane_ready` event plus tmux metadata), selectors, normal and here placement through owned caller panes, conflicts, retained panes. Use hand-built fixed agent-args/settings fixtures for the spawn check (this checks the Gashki merge mechanism without the adapter's argument generator).
5. Record which mechanisms the proof covers and which live vendor facts remain unverified (effective dontAsk mode, merged rule order, refusal of out-of-scope writes with a real vendor CLI).

Outputs: a tier-B preparation record and a reproducible isolated fixture.

Fixtures used: F-GK-REAL (pinned release-style Gashki, separate gashkitest build for named seams, isolated tmux/config/state roots, owned hook-capable vendor stubs, both planner assignments, normal/here placement).
acceptance_criteria:
Done when: no fixture path can resolve to a real vendor binary; the fixture server and roots are owned; the pinned contract subset and ready-event/socket evidence are checked before any adapter depends on them.
- A-GK-01 (tier B, F-GK-REAL): prepare separate release-style/gashkitest binaries, isolated server/config/roots and prove provider PATH. Try both fault/hold triggers on the release-style binary. Required: both build hashes/tags and the exact contract subset checked. Release triggers are inert, with no injected failure/hold; no assumed refusal error. No real vendor path can be selected. The fixture owns roots/socket/cleanup targets. Covers U08, C11, C13, C14.
- A-GK-02 (tier B, F-GK-REAL): spawn both providers/roles with fixed hand-built agent-args/settings fixtures, tools, models, effort, normal/here placement and folder trust. This checks the Gashki merge mechanism without the Volley argument generator. Required: captured argv/settings retain hooks and role rules, a valid ready event/socket and pane UUID. dontAsk enforcement is not claimed from stubs. Covers baseline, C12, C15, D06.
- Evidence rules for every case: report ID, tier, fixture, stimulus variant, source/binary hashes, settings, target OS, observed output, artifact hashes and process/paste counts. For tier B, assert real Gashki results and stub hook/paste counts independently. A plan, a source comment, or a stub that merely returns the required answer is not evidence.
notes: DONE: A-GK-01 and A-GK-02 passed with pinned release and gashkitest builds on macOS arm64 and Linux arm64. Each OS run passed 12 Go test results across ten owned fixtures. Independent records show 19 agent processes (17 accepted turns plus two refused startups), 17 pastes and 51 hooks per OS. Both planner assignments, normal/here placement, folder trust, exact merged role rules, ready UUID/socket/cursor, retained panes, conflicts and selectors passed. Absent-provider and unapproved/wrong-path trust cases refused safely. Release fault and hold triggers were inert; the tagged fault build returned INTERNAL. Evidence SHA-256: 07278e09bc3d46871d4cc16d21343bf77d252d57c087b17939b0979aec5fa063. Failed narrow-pane attempts remain; passing geometry is 320x60. Full isolated Go suite, vet and diff checks passed. No live vendor conversation ran. Vendor permission enforcement remains a T24 gate.

title: T13 Implement the checked Gashki backend
description: Why: the Gashki backend drives persistent agent panes through the Gashki tool instead of one process per turn. That raises hard questions the Bash engine answers loosely (C09, C11): was a prompt delivered, did a lost reply mean it was pasted, is this the same pane and server as before, which completion event belongs to which send? The Go adapter must treat every Gashki result as strictly checked evidence, use only the public contract (never Gashki's private ledger), recover a lost send acknowledgment only through the same-key public call, and hand over to the user rather than ever guess. It supplies primitive pane operations; it contains no round loop.
design:
Work: build provider agent-args JSON arrays and the single Claude settings object (model/effort, tools, read roots, role-specific path rules; Claude role/backend rules: planner under Gashki gets planner list, same planner path rule, protected denies and checked read roots; critic/advisory gets critic list plus required Write, same read roots and `Edit(//<absolute-workspace-without-leading-slash>/rounds/**)` only). Preserve the Gashki hook-merge contract: never duplicate Gashki's hook installation or replace its mandatory settings JSON. Implement unique selectors, owned spawn reconciliation, payload/key binding, strict send classification, cursor-qualified waits, fixed total deadlines, server checks, pane retention and cleanup intents. Preserve unsupported or uncertain upstream evidence. Supply primitive pane operations through the executor interface; call the frozen-config hash gate before every Gashki subprocess; declare exact output/control observations. The integration task owns the real executor wiring.

1. Calls and JSON. Pass the frozen `--config=PATH` on every Gashki call after records are committed. Query mechanism state from Gashki; do not reconstruct it from retired variables. All subprocess JSON is bounded, strict and checked against the required contract subset. A successful exit with malformed JSON is not a successful action. Preserve raw response, stderr, exit status and parse/validation errors.
2. IDs and ownership. Run ID: 128 random bits, 26 lowercase unpadded base32 characters, alphabet a-z2-7; check collisions under creation ownership before mutation. Group `vly-<run-id>` (30 characters, fits Gashki's 32-character limit). Pane names `planner`, `critic`, `second`. Never put workspace basenames or user text in selectors. Validate generated names; a generator defect is INTERNAL. Persist spawn intent with selector, provider, cwd, placement, agent-argument hash, config hash and expected ownership. A fresh run never adopts an existing pane merely because its name matches. On resume the returned pane UUID must equal the saved UUID, and its matching ready event, agent, selector and saved server identity must validate before send. A lost spawn response may permit one same-selector reconciliation call only when preparation proves the intended run owns that selector; accept `existing=true` only with a matching `pane_ready` event and a usable ready observation; otherwise hand over without killing a pane of uncertain ownership.
3. Socket and server. Read the actual socket path from matching `pane_ready` evidence and checked tmux metadata; canonicalize path aliases before comparison. An unset Gashki socket setting does not prove the selected server is the old server. On resume check the selected server against the saved actual server before observe/send/kill. A different server is SERVER_CONFLICT even if a pane appears not found there. Unknown socket identity is an explicit handover condition.
4. Placement and arguments. `placement=auto` uses here only when a valid TMUX/TMUX_PANE caller is present, otherwise normal. `normal` does not pass here. `here` requires a valid caller and checked matching server. Save caller window identity for a here run and keep Gashki's same-window conflict behavior; a rerun in another window cannot silently move or replace old panes. Provider agent arguments are one JSON array of strings. Claude gets requested model/effort, context directory, one settings object, dontAsk, and the allowed file/Skill tools; its critic has no Edit or command tools. Codex gets requested model/effort and Gashki's declared workspace-write/approval behavior. The Codex planner is workspace-write with detection only; a Gashki Codex critic has a weaker write boundary (a pane remains workspace-write), so the protected-set check applies after every turn on each backend. The guide must state that detection does not prevent changes during a turn, that crash recovery trusts validated records on disk (coordinated alteration of a manifest and a matching transaction can evade the checks), and that the inbox journal checks consistency, not writer identity (a Codex planner with workspace-write could forge a receipt and journal entry).
5. Send contract. Before send, save an immutable rendered prompt, pointer payload and their hashes. Use a unique turn path containing run ID and turn ID so transcript matches cannot select a prior turn. The pointer payload is one line naming that full path. Bind the send key to run ID, logical turn ID, pane UUID, provider-session evidence, config hash and pointer payload hash. Hash the exact Gashki-normalized payload (trim ASCII space, tab, CR, LF at both ends).

| Send result | Action |
| --- | --- |
| valid ok, submitted=true, matching payload hash, expected pane, non-empty turn_cursor, no unverified warning (replayed permitted) | save confirmed receipt and cursor; await the matching turn |
| SEND_UNCONFIRMED, SEND_STUCK_IN_COMPOSER, SEND_INTERRUPTED, SEND_INPUT_MIXED, including replayed evidence | save any barrier cursor; SEND_UNCERTAIN; handover |
| NOT_SAFE_TO_SEND with checked refusal before paste | wait for safe idle within remaining budget, then send with the same key and payload; no-paste evidence mandatory |
| COMPOSER_NOT_EMPTY with checked refusal before paste | SEND_UNCERTAIN handover; never clear the composer |
| PANE_DEAD with checked refusal before paste | SESSION_LOST; retain records |
| missing or lost send receipt | checked same-key recovery (below) before handover |
| SUBMIT_UNVERIFIED, empty/missing cursor, malformed response, hash mismatch | SEND_UNCERTAIN; retain intent and pane; handover |
| IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT | stop with binding conflict; never choose a different key to bypass it |

Checked refusal-before-paste evidence: a strict, bound response from the send verb with NOT_SAFE_TO_SEND, COMPOSER_NOT_EMPTY or PANE_DEAD, no `barrier_cursor` and no `submit_evidence` in data or error evidence. The no-paste guarantee is established by the pinned Gashki send source refusal/finish path and its guide (checked in the fixture task and A-GK-09); the capabilities listing alone does not state it. Absence of a cursor alone never proves no paste. A refusal code from wait/observe is not this send guarantee. Contradictory fields or an unchecked binary/contract yield SEND_UNCERTAIN and forbid automatic retry.
6. Same-key recovery for a missing/lost receipt. First settle any prior owned send subprocess and acquire the owner lock. Verify the saved key, pane UUID, exact normalized payload hash, frozen Gashki config/hash, queried state_dir and actual server identity. If any binding cannot be verified, hand over without a send call. Otherwise repeat the public send call with the same key and exact payload; never allocate a new key. Use a recovery attempt record under the same logical turn, keeping original evidence. Gashki replays a terminal result, closes an open post-barrier attempt as interrupted without paste, and can start a new attempt only when the old attempt was abandoned/refused before any paste. Apply the send table to the recovered result: a recovered confirmed cursor advances to wait; an interrupted or unverified result cannot. A further lost recovery response retains bindings for a later explicit resume (no unbounded retry loop). This covers a crash before the first send call and a crash after its return but before receipt save. Never replay an already classified malformed response automatically. Never call send with no-verify. Never read Gashki's private send ledger. A saved confirmed cursor is awaited again without another send.
7. Wait contract. Call wait with `until=idle` and `since=<saved turn cursor>`. Validate returned pane, state, cursor, event evidence and expected turn ordering. An idle screen without the turn's completion evidence is not completion. A finite turn budget includes send/confirmation and wait time; compute remaining time. Gashki's declared wait duration is 1s through 24h. If remaining finite budget is under 1s, treat it as exhausted and return TURN_TIMEOUT without calling Gashki wait; do not round up beyond the budget (this applies to a 500ms budget and no-paste recovery waits). Use chunks within that range keeping the same original cursor; the process deadline still enforces the total budget. With an unlimited budget, continue after a checked wait timeout only when the owned pane remains working or compacting with no terminal failure. With a finite exhausted budget, preserve the pane and return TURN_TIMEOUT/handover. Approval-required, dead-pane, auth or turn-failure results preserve cursor evidence and hand over; never press approval keys automatically.
8. Recovery and cleanup. A resume after confirmed delivery and lost result re-waits using the saved cursor (no spawn/send as a substitute). A missing main pane is SESSION_LOST when its session cannot be restored through checked public evidence; never spawn a blank planner/critic pane under the old logical session identity. Gashki's public spawn/observe responses do not expose the vendor session ID; transcript-derived IDs are nullable observations, not interchangeable with pane UUIDs. On approved completion or impasse, commit cleanup intent for only the run's verified owned role panes; kill through the frozen config and saved server identity; a checked already-dead/not-found owned pane is idempotent completion; a cleanup error records `cleanup_pending` with a warning and safe follow-up commands, without erasing the final artifact or claiming panes were removed. On uncertainty, timeout or unverified ownership keep panes by default. Explicit cleanup names exactly those panes and retains all files and receipts.
9. Native mapping of Gashki outcomes. Use the pinned capabilities registry, verb source and saved action context together. Keep upstream code, exit, message, evidence, cursor, verb and binary/contract hashes in the native receipt. Never copy Gashki's retryable flag into Volley's exit policy. "no new turn" means no new loop-requested prompt (a spawned vendor process can still exist); "retain" means retain any verified owned pane and records and never kill a pane with unknown ownership. Context rules before mapping: a proven server/pane binding mismatch is SERVER_CONFLICT or PANE_CONFLICT (exit 5) before any call; if send may have crossed its barrier and the response does not prove its outcome, use SEND_UNCERTAIN (exit 8) rather than a safe input/environment/transient mapping; a missing send receipt uses the same-key recovery first and a saved confirmed cursor survives wait/observe errors; a prerequisite error while recovering an unfinished non-send action is TURN_UNCERTAIN (exit 8) unless the table names a more specific terminal/session failure; after final approval/impasse a kill failure records CLEANUP_PENDING and retains the final result/exit (the mapped code is diagnostic evidence, not a new failed verdict); NOT_FOUND/PANE_DEAD on cleanup is success only when checked ownership and death/absence evidence prove that the exact saved pane is gone on the saved server, otherwise retain cleanup_pending. The table (upstream code and call context -> native code / exit; turn evidence; pane policy):
   - UNKNOWN_FLAG, UNKNOWN_COMMAND, INVALID_INPUT, MISSING_REQUIRED from a generated checked call -> UPSTREAM_FAILURE / 8; no new turn only when validation refusal is verified; retain; adapter/protocol investigation; never silently change argv or retry.
   - INVALID_CONFIG from a frozen/selected config read -> INVALID_CONFIG / 3; no new turn; retain existing panes; fix prerequisite without changing frozen records (a detected frozen hash change uses ARTIFACT_CHANGED / 5 instead).
   - TMUX_NO_SERVER, TMUX_TOO_OLD, AGENT_CLI_MISSING before an action with no unfinished turn -> DEPENDENCY_MISSING / 3; proven no new turn; retain; no replacement pane.
   - STATE_DIR_UNWRITABLE during preparation before external action -> DEPENDENCY_MISSING / 3; proven no new turn; retain; no dependent action until storage works.
   - STATE_DIR_UNWRITABLE after spawn/send/kill invocation -> UPSTREAM_FAILURE / 8 (subject to the send-uncertainty rule); action completion can be unknown; retain; reconcile only through the public contract; no safe retry from code alone.
   - AGENT_NOT_LOGGED_IN, CODEX_HOOKS_UNTRUSTED, LAUNCH_PROMPT_UNHANDLED -> UPSTREAM_FAILURE / 8; no confirmed review turn at spawn (process can exist); during wait retain old delivery facts; retain; manual investigation; no automatic key press.
   - HERE_UNAVAILABLE -> PANE_CONFLICT / 5; no confirmed new turn; partial spawn evidence may remain; retain; use the declared caller/server/window repair; never move or replace existing panes.
   - TMUX_SPLIT_FAILED -> EXECUTION_ENVIRONMENT_FAILED / 3; no confirmed new turn; preserve partial spawn evidence; retain; save tmux stderr and window dimensions; enlarge a too-small window before a checked same-selector reconciliation; not an identity conflict.
   - CONFLICT for agent, dead existing selector or here-window mismatch -> PANE_CONFLICT / 5; no new prompt; retain; no adoption or replacement.
   - IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT -> IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT / 5; no new action; old action not proved complete; retain; never bypass with a new key.
   - NOT_FOUND from send/wait/observe for a saved pane -> SESSION_LOST / 8; old turn may have run; retain records; no blank replacement. A discovery-only missing read uses NOT_FOUND / 1.
   - PANE_DEAD from send/wait/observe -> SESSION_LOST / 8; send refusal is no-paste only with the checked refusal-before-paste evidence; wait can follow a prior turn; retain records and death/cursor evidence.
   - COMPOSER_NOT_EMPTY from send -> SEND_UNCERTAIN / 8; no new paste only with refusal evidence; do not clear the composer.
   - NOT_SAFE_TO_SEND from send -> internal no-paste recovery (no outward failure until budget/other result); proven no paste only with the evidence above; wait for safe idle then same-key send within budget; budget expiry gives TURN_TIMEOUT / 8.
   - LOCKED before a proven not-started send/kill or read -> LOCKED / 4; refused call made no new mutation; bounded wait/retry only for that call with same key/bindings; unfinished old action uses uncertainty rules.
   - APPROVAL_REQUIRED -> TURN_FAILED / 8 with reason=approval_required; prior turn may be pending; retain pane and cursor; hand over; never press approval keys or use exit 4 to retry the model turn.
   - TURN_FAILED -> TURN_FAILED / 8 with reason=upstream_turn_failed; retain pane/cursor/error evidence; hand over.
   - WAIT_TIMEOUT during finite-budget turn/settlement -> TURN_TIMEOUT / 8 when the total budget is exhausted, otherwise continue bounded chunks; retain original cursor; never resend.
   - WAIT_TIMEOUT during an unlimited turn -> continue only under the working/compacting rule, else TURN_UNCERTAIN / 8; no default hidden limit.
   - SEND_STUCK_IN_COMPOSER, SEND_UNCONFIRMED, SEND_INTERRUPTED, SEND_INPUT_MIXED -> SEND_UNCERTAIN / 8; retain pane and barrier cursor including replayed evidence; no new key, no no-verify.
   - AGENT_UNVERIFIABLE -> UPSTREAM_FAILURE / 8; refused send, no supported submit proof; never add no-verify.
   - ENV_NOT_SET, CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED -> UPSTREAM_FAILURE / 8; generated call violates the prepared contract; retain; never export an assumed identity root or add acknowledgment automatically.
   - INTERNAL, CONFORMANCE_FAILED from Gashki -> UPSTREAM_FAILURE / 8 (subject to the send-uncertainty rule); native INTERNAL / 6 is reserved for a Volley defect.
   - TTY_REQUIRED, CONFIG_UNWRITABLE, EDITOR_FAILED, DATA_DIR_UNWRITABLE -> UPSTREAM_FAILURE / 8; not reachable through the declared subset; unexpected-response investigation.
   - SUBMIT_UNVERIFIED warning -> SEND_UNCERTAIN / 8; never accept a completion receipt.
   - HOOK_SCREEN_DISAGREE, HOOK_STREAM_GAP warnings -> no standalone native error; preserve warning evidence; enforce known-field/cursor/completion checks; if proof is insufficient, TURN_UNCERTAIN / 8.
   - PANE_LABEL_UNAVAILABLE, EVENT_LOG_LARGE, ENV_SETTING_IGNORED, DEPRECATED warnings -> no standalone native error; preserve warning evidence; warning cannot replace required proof.
   Unknown codes, wrong-verb codes or invalid envelopes use UPSTREAM_FAILURE / 8, or SEND_UNCERTAIN / 8 when send may have occurred. Never infer safety from an upstream exit value alone.

Outputs: Gashki adapter with typed outcomes and no private-ledger access. Include matching provider/UUID/cursor fields in every accepted receipt.

Fixtures used: F-GK-CANNED (owned Gashki process stub with canned envelopes, call records, simulated pane/server bindings), F-GK-REAL (pinned release-style Gashki with isolated tmux, separate gashkitest build for named seams, owned hook-capable vendor stubs, both planner assignments, normal/here), F-PURE for argument generation.

Done when: a lost receipt first uses checked same-key recovery; malformed or cursor-less results hand over; a saved confirmed cursor resumes through wait only; a missing persistent pane does not become a blank session.

title: T14 Implement bounded final-reply and transcript extraction
description: Why: after a planner turn the user wants the planner's conversational reply recorded, but the reply is secondary evidence. Under the direct backend it comes from owned output; under Gashki it must be found in the vendor's own transcript files, which are shared, large and private. Picking "the newest transcript" would silently attach another conversation's text to this turn (the Bash engine did this kind of guess, C01). This task builds reply extraction that only trusts an exact unique prompt-path marker in the checked vendor root, parses only supported record forms, and reports late, missing, unsupported, read-failed or ambiguous replies honestly instead of inventing text. A missing planner reply must never block a run whose requested artifact is valid; a missing required critic artifact always blocks.
design:
Work: capture direct replies from owned outputs and Gashki replies from exact prompt-path matches in checked roots. Parse only supported Claude/Codex record forms. Distinguish late, missing, unsupported, read-failed and ambiguous replies. Save reply result and reason in turn receipts.

1. Direct sources. Direct Claude final text comes from owned print output. Direct Codex final text comes from the owned last-message path and the checked event protocol. The engine never asks the planner to create response files. A required critic reply is different: it is an artifact needed for review progression and stays mandatory.
2. Gashki transcript location. Locate transcript candidates only under the checked vendor root and workspace/session identity context. Use the exact immutable prompt-path marker (the unique turn path containing run ID and turn ID that the Gashki backend put in the pointer payload) to locate the turn. Never choose the newest modified transcript as the only binding proof.
3. Extraction rules. Claude extraction stops at the next typed user prompt and selects final assistant text for the matched turn. Codex extraction selects the first completion event for the matched user prompt and rejects a later unrelated completion. Unknown record variants remain `unsupported-format`; they are not silently parsed as empty success. Ambiguous multiple matches are unavailable evidence, not an arbitrary newest-file choice.
4. Bounded capture. Retry reply discovery for a bounded 2-second capture interval after checked completion (use an injected clock). Then save `REPLY_UNAVAILABLE` with status and reason if the requested spec is valid. Never invent reply text or silently copy the spec as the conversational reply. Reply result values: found, pending, unsupported-format, missing, read-failed. A missing/pending reply can warn; a missing required artifact cannot be waived.
5. Receipt contents. Keep root paths and observed format/version facts in the receipt. Never copy complete unrelated vendor histories into the workspace. Fixtures contain tiny vendor-format samples with no private conversation material.

Outputs: transcript adapters and small vendor-format fixtures; reply result and reason saved in turn receipts.

Fixtures used: F-FILES (owned temporary workspace plus exact-byte files, hashes and a fake clock).

title: T15 Implement question generations and input receipts
description: Why: when the planner has an open question for the user, the review must stop and wait for a human answer without losing, misreading or double-applying it. The Bash engine decides a user answered by file modification times, takes half-written answers, and can reapply an answer after a crash (C02). The Go engine binds each question to a random generation ID, records exact bytes and a baseline observation of the answer file, accepts answers only through an immutable receipt with a durable journal commit, and applies each accepted input exactly once as one logical application (external delivery is never blindly retried). A waiting run must not block submissions, so submissions use their own short inbox lock.
design:
Work: implement exact answer/steering commands, generation IDs, strict bounded stdin, direct-file observations, terminal input, question withdrawal, immutable archives, and Gashki answer-turn settlement. Use the inbox lock and the state task's journal protocol so a waiting owner does not block submissions. Acknowledge only durable journal commits and preserve keyed retry identity after an interrupted submission. Implement answer settlement against a fake pane/guard interface and own its unit case A-HUMAN-06 (real Gashki settlement is A-HUMAN-04 in the integration task; the whole-loop wait behavior A-HUMAN-05 belongs to the review-engine task).

1. Question rules. Only the planner writes open questions: numbered, with options and a recommendation, the recommendation used provisionally in SPEC.md. When none remain, QUESTIONS.md is absent or empty (whitespace-only is empty; headings and answered-question records are not empty).
2. Generations. After a completed planner turn, read a stable question file and bind its exact bytes/hash to a random question generation ID. Save the originating turn, the next review round, and a baseline observation of HUMAN.md. An observation contains existence, canonical path, device/inode, length and content hash. Modification time is diagnostic only and is never the ownership rule. A pre-existing HUMAN.md with unchanged observation is not a new answer.
3. Direct file answers. File watching accepts a changed HUMAN.md observation after the generation begins. A replaced file with the same bytes has a new identity and counts as a new submission. A same-byte write to the same inode cannot be distinguished reliably; document `human answer` as the exact method there. Require two equal complete reads separated by the declared poll interval before consuming an external file. Invalid UTF-8, non-regular files, oversized files and a changing file remain pending or produce a declared answer conflict. Never take half an append as the final answer. Use the command path for exact completion rather than promising that debounce proves an arbitrary writer finished.
4. Archiving. Snapshot the question bytes, answer bytes and prior directive bytes before archiving. Do not remove a source file unless it still matches the consumed observation; if it changed, retain it for the next boundary and report pending input. Archive writes are idempotent under generation/receipt IDs. A crash between copy, commit and source removal must not lose or reapply the accepted input.
5. Commands. `human answer --from-stdin` reads one JSON object with required `text` and optional `idempotency_key`; `--file` reads exact UTF-8 answer text from one regular file. Both require the current question ID and produce an immutable answer receipt. Limit question, answer, steering and patch inputs to 1 MiB each. Never trim or summarize the user's words; preserve line breaks in the archived answer body. A repeated key with identical text returns the existing receipt; the same key with different text is IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT. A stale question ID is ANSWER_CONFLICT and cannot advance the run. `human steer` reads a JSON object with required `text` and optional `idempotency_key` and records a one-shot directive for the next safe boundary; it does not answer an existing question implicitly. The owner displays pending steering while waiting but continues to block on an unanswered question. A direct HUMAN.md file can supply both the awaited answer and prior steering (legacy channel); the receipt states that interpretation. `human skip` (needs `--yes`) acknowledges withdrawal of the current question; deleting or emptying QUESTIONS.md after the wait starts means the same. Record the original question and the withdrawal; it is not an answer or approval of the recommended choice. The planner must remove the question and retain any choice as a proposal; a binding requirement conflict can be raised again by a later review. Deleting a question file never bypasses explicit user requirements.
6. Inbox protocol (from the state task): under the short inbox lock save and sync an immutable input receipt, then append and sync its commit to `state/inputs/inbox.jsonl` before acknowledgment. A receipt without a journal commit is pending evidence and cannot release a gate. An identical keyed retry may finish its journal commit; a conflicting retry is refused. First committed answer wins; a typed losing candidate is retained separately and reported as not applied.
7. Gashki planner-pane answer settlement. With Gashki the planner also lists questions at the end of its visible reply. The answer turn only adds the user's answer word for word to HUMAN.md and must not change SPEC.md or QUESTIONS.md. A clarifying exchange without a completed answer does not release the gate. No loop-requested turn starts while that answer turn is active. When an answer file arrives, observe the planner pane before consuming it: if working, save the observation cursor and wait for a subsequent idle event using `--since`; if already safely idle, record that observation and verify stable answer files; if completion cannot be established, retain the answer receipt and enter handover. Hash SPEC.md and QUESTIONS.md around this settlement; unexpected answer-turn edits create a conflict. Never use an unqualified idle wait to complete a loop-requested turn whose cursor is missing; the current-state observation is only for settling a user-started answer turn. Pane settlement takes a backend interface (the integration task checks it against the real Gashki backend).
8. Terminal input. Controller interactive input accumulates lines until an empty line, then appends after a prior directive through one atomic write or submits a receipt. If another answer wins first, retain the typed candidate separately and report it was not applied. EOF ends terminal input; it does not submit an empty answer or release the question.
9. Applying a directive exactly once. An accepted answer or steering receipt schedules a planner application turn before the next critic round. The prompt includes the exact archived question and answer where applicable; the critic sees the same archived directive in that round. Record application intent, receipt and both role deliveries by receipt ID. A controller crash cannot select a new logical application under a new turn ID. External model delivery is not guaranteed exactly once after a lost result; the guarantee is one committed logical application plus no blind delivery retry. For Gashki first use the bound same-key receipt recovery; if evidence remains uncertain, hand over instead of repeating the answer turn.

Outputs: human package, input schemas, archive transactions, fixtures for stale/identical/concurrent answers. Preserve the answer-turn no-edit rule.

Fixtures used: F-FILES; F-PURE (fake pane/guard interface).

Two stable reads, no mtime ownership. The same-inode same-byte limitation directs the user to `human answer`. Covers C02.

Source removed only if the observation matches; later input stays pending. No loss or second selection. Covers C01, C02, C08.

Required: unit settlement waits for qualified completion, preserves the exact answer, refuses edits, and returns a typed handover without starting a loop turn. Real pane behavior is A-HUMAN-04 in the integration task. Covers C02, C08, C15.
- Evidence rules for every case: report ID, tier, fixture, stimulus variant, source/binary hashes, settings, target OS, observed output, artifact hashes. A plan, a source comment, or a stub that merely returns the required answer is not evidence.

title: T16 Implement the ordinary review transition engine
description: Why: this is the heart of the conversion. The Bash loop decides what happens next by counting files and comparing modification times, and it treats a missing verdict, a lost process or a half-written spec loosely (C01, C04, C05, C07). The Go engine replaces that with pure transition rules over one committed checkpoint, plus an effect-driving owner loop in which every external effect has a committed intent and every advancement has a validated receipt. It also introduces the single guarded turn executor that compares the protected set around every agent turn, so no backend adapter can bypass tamper detection. The first runnable slice uses direct stub agents; the integration task later extends the same engine to the Gashki backend.
design:
Work: implement seeded/draft start, directive application before critique, strict final-line verdicts, one retry, conservative missing-verdict handling, revisions, snapshots, questions, cap amendments, impasse and explicit unfinished-turn recovery. Build the `GuardedTurnExecutor` that owns the pre/post protected-inventory comparison around every role, purpose, backend and successful/failed turn, using the comparator from the state task and the hash gate from the records task; adapters remain primitive operations. Check PLANNER_MUTATION, CRITIC_MUTATION, reserved output names, registered sinks and exact `state/control/` deltas before accepting a result. Connect minimal direct `run`/`resume` handlers to the declared machine-contract response so this task supplies a runnable slice; the command-handler task completes the rest of the command tree. Design rule: review package is pure (no I/O); the owner loop drives effects.

1. Statuses (user-facing condition): `ready` (a safe next operation exists, no active owner); `running` (owner preparing or awaiting a checked turn); `awaiting_answer` (a question generation needs a user decision); `handover` (delivery, completion, identity or process evidence needs investigation); `impasse` (no final approval within the round cap); `approved` (final bytes have the required completed approval basis); `stopped` (explicit stop or abandonment). Phases (next logical operation): prepare, draft, apply_directive, critique, critique_retry, revise, await_answer, second_opinion, closing, confirm_closing, commit_final, cleanup. A phase also has a turn-operation state: prepared, intent_committed, delivery_confirmed, completion_observed, receipt_saved, result_committed. A separate `delivery_uncertain` flag with evidence is never called completed.
2. Main transitions: Fresh brief + no spec: commit draft intent, request planner draft, validate, then answer gate or critique round 1. Fresh seeded spec: save initial spec hash and input snapshot; critique round 1; no draft turn. Pending applicable human directive: archive input, request planner application; review the changed spec at the scheduled critic round. Critique REVISE: save critique and reviewed spec hash; planner revision, snapshot, answer gate. Critique missing verdict: save the first reply; ask once with a reminder; valid verdict or recorded MISSING. Retry still MISSING: save both attempts and a diagnostic; conservative revision; next round or impasse. Critique APPROVE: save the exact approval basis (advisory/closing passes are the next task). Cap exhausted before needed review: save reason and open questions; impasse, never an unreviewed final approval.
3. Rounds. A round is one ordinary critic turn plus its one possible verdict reminder and the required planner response. Draft, directive application, second opinion and closing do not consume an ordinary critic round (they are recorded as turns with purpose; costs unknown unless observed). The closing confirmation uses another ordinary round and counts toward the cap. A final-round REVISE can still receive its planner revision, but the resulting spec is not approved. Do not wait for answers when the cap provides no next critic round; record the question in `state/IMPASSE.md` and offer a higher-cap resume.
4. Verdict grammar. Normalize CRLF to LF for parsing only, keeping exact saved critique bytes. Ignore trailing blank lines only. The final non-empty line must be exactly `VERDICT: APPROVE` or `VERDICT: REVISE`. Reject Markdown fences, prefixes, quoted examples, lower-case words, trailing comments and substring matches elsewhere. Record the parsed verdict, artifact hash, line number and parser version. One reminder turn uses a new logical attempt ID, does not overwrite the first reply, refers to the missing final line and preserves the common review rule and binding inputs. If the reminder also lacks a verdict, save MISSING and continue conservatively to revision within the round budget. A missing verdict can never terminate approval. The planner receives the missing-verdict diagnostic with the actual critique.
5. Binding inputs and external edits. At each safe boundary snapshot the brief, constraints, spec, applicable human inputs, prompts and requested context identity. A changing brief or constraint file after freeze is a conflict; do not silently mix versions across roles. A human directive can request a deliberate new brief version, but the engine must record the amendment and recheck before approval. A user edit to SPEC.md while an owned turn is active gives ARTIFACT_CHANGED unless the expected planner is its writer. The next safe manual resume can accept an explicit spec amendment through a recorded command and a new critique boundary. A critic changing SPEC.md is CRITIC_MUTATION whether or not its verdict approves. A human write after the final input snapshot is not retroactively included; report pending unconsumed input when the final commit notices it before completion.
6. Guarded executor. Before each turn: inventory the protected set (state/**, frozen configs, BRIEF.md, CONSTRAINTS.md, existing committed rounds artifacts), record the journal head, register exact sinks and control receipts. After each completed or failed turn compare before trusting a receipt or starting another action. Planner change: PLANNER_MUTATION (exit 8) with actor, paths, before/after observations and retained evidence; critic change: CRITIC_MUTATION (exit 8); external/unknown writer: ARTIFACT_CHANGED with actor external_or_unknown. A frozen-config mismatch suppresses the launch with ARTIFACT_CHANGED / 5. Controller signals checkpoint with exit 130/143 where possible. The same executor serves auxiliary purposes later.
7. Attachments (`run` on an existing workspace). `run` creates or attaches to the workspace's one current run; the canonical physical workspace is the natural creation key. An optional `--idempotency-key` also binds to the resolved request hash. An attachment loads frozen settings first; explicit settings must match; an absent flag does not re-resolve ambient defaults. The request hash includes resolved settings, seed source identities, prompt set, canonical context and active executable/identity bindings; it excludes rendering, answer-wait controls and the current output SPEC.md bytes. A key bound to a different request returns IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT; with no key or an unbound new key a differing request returns CONFIG_CONFLICT (no new key is saved on failure); a matching new key can be bound to the existing request under the lock without creating a run. Saved status and matching `run` action: ready: acquire the owner lock and execute the safe next step (as `runs resume` without amendments); running with live owner: LOCKED with the same run handle, never a second owner; running with no owner: acquire the lock and apply backend recovery (never infer the agent stopped); awaiting_answer: acquire the lock and check receipts, return ANSWER_REQUIRED or wait; handover: attempt only declared recovery, an unresolved boundary returns its recorded handover code; approved: return the saved result with zero agent calls after saved-state integrity checks; impasse: REVIEW_IMPASSE, a higher-cap `runs resume` is needed; stopped: CONFIG_CONFLICT and a fresh-workspace command, never restart. A changed actual identity or binary on attachment fails its specific binding check before execution, never resets artifacts or creates a second run. `--brief=PATH` can seed an absent BRIEF.md; `--seed=PATH` can seed an absent SPEC.md in a fresh workspace; refuse a different existing target; matching bytes are an idempotent no-op; both seed sources together are contradictory.
8. Resume. `runs resume` uses committed settings and the current manifest. Permitted changes: a higher `--max-rounds` and observation controls. A flag matching the frozen value is accepted; a differing model, effort, role, backend, prompt set, context path, permission setting, identity context or binary binding is refused. A lower cap is refused. A higher cap is a versioned run-control amendment that does not rewrite the original settings record. A terminal approved run returns its existing result without agent calls. An impasse resumes only with a higher cap and a safe next boundary.
9. Question wait behavior. A native foreground run makes model turns synchronously until completion or a recorded handover; it does not detach a worker. At an unanswered question the default returns ANSWER_REQUIRED (exit 8) with the run ID and answer commands. With `--wait` it watches answer inputs without requesting another agent turn. `--interactive` additionally permits controller-terminal answers; it requires `--wait`, terminal stdin, human rendering and no other stdin consumer, and is incompatible with `--json`. Without `--interactive`, stdin never triggers a prompt or answer reader. The run's `--wait-timeout` is the per-turn execution budget (on `runs get`/`runs events` the same spelling is a read-wait budget; capabilities and help must state the distinction); there is no total review deadline, no user-answer deadline, and no hidden finite default.
10. Interrupted/unfinished turns: after owner death, recovery trusts validated records; never infer completion from a non-empty artifact; a lost direct delivery hands over (never an automatic repeat); no replacement turn from a partial spec.

Outputs: pure transition rules, the common guarded turn executor, and an effect-driving owner loop. Every effect has a committed intent; every advancement has a validated receipt.

Fixtures used: F-DIRECT (owned Claude/Codex stubs with captured argv, null-stdin checks, event/reply scripts, launch counts; both planner assignments; one-shot and persistent); F-FILES.

- A-LOOP-01 (tier A, F-DIRECT): brief-only and seeded-spec starts with REVISE then APPROVE. Required: brief drafts; seed goes directly to critique. Required revision and snapshot precede the next critique; no file-count state inference. Both role assignments work. Covers baseline, C01.
- A-LOOP-02 (tier A, F-DIRECT): exact final verdict; embedded/quoted/fenced/lower-case/trailing-comment verdicts; CRLF; reminder succeeds or fails. Required: only the exact final non-empty line is accepted. The separate retry is retained. Two missing verdicts record MISSING and a conservative revision, never a received REVISE or approval. Covers C04, C05.
- A-LOOP-03 (tier A, F-DIRECT): pending directive before the critic would approve; crash during application/receipt save. Required: planner applies the exact input first. title: T17 Implement advisory review, closing, and final approval
description: Why: after a critic first approves, the Bash engine decides whether to run an extra "closing" planner pass by searching the critique text for trigger words (C06), and it can finalize a spec that was changed after approval without a fresh review (C07). The Go engine runs at most one fresh advisory critique and at most one eligible closing pass per run, decides eligibility by round budget instead of keywords, requires a new ordinary critic APPROVE for any changed bytes, and records an exact final approval basis before cleanup. If optional closing changes cannot be confirmed within the round cap, it can safely return to the already approved bytes, but only under strict unchanged-input and settled-turn checks. This task waits for the reply-extraction and Gashki-backend tasks so final reply capture has one checked interface for both backends; the earlier direct ordinary loop stays runnable with auxiliary passes disabled.
design:
Work: implement one fresh advisory session and at most one eligible closing pass per run. Save the approved snapshot and the no-round-left skip record. Remove remark keyword tests. Compare pre/post closing hashes and require a new ordinary critic round when bytes change. Commit the exact final approval basis before cleanup. Implement the guarded rejected-at-cap restoration and its crash recovery. Auxiliary purposes run through the same guarded executor as ordinary turns.

1. Second opinion (setting `second_opinion`). Runs once after the first ordinary approval, if enabled. Its vendor session is fresh even when the two main roles use persistent sessions. It cannot change the ordinary verdict. Save its complete critique at `rounds/second-opinion.md` and bind it to the spec hash it saw. The advisory critic gets the same rubric and an explicit advisory scope.
2. Closing pass (setting `closing_pass`, default true). Runs at most once after the approval and advisory result, if enabled and an ordinary confirmation round remains. If no round remains, record `closing_skipped: no_round_left` and finalize the approved bytes after input-stability checks; keep advisory notes in the final result; a skipped pass never turns APPROVE into impasse. Before a closing launch, atomically save exact approved bytes at `rounds/closing-approved.spec.md`; bind its hash and the ordinary approval receipt in the closing intent; retain the snapshot through changed closing bytes, failed turns, questions and impasse; restore it only through the guarded decision below, never overwriting an unrecorded edit. The closing prompt reads both reviews and permits addressing or declining optional notes. No keyword search decides whether it runs. Cost to document: one planner turn per eligible approved run, and at least one critic turn when closing changes bytes; a confirmation REVISE can need further ordinary revisions and critic turns within the cap. If no optional point needs a change, closing can leave the spec unchanged. The tool captures its reply at `rounds/closing-response.md`.
3. Outcomes. Closing leaves unchanged spec and no question: commit the closing receipt; final approval after the input-stability check. Closing changes spec: save snapshot and pending final hash; next ordinary critic round as `confirm_closing`. confirm_closing returns REVISE or retry ends MISSING: normal planner revision, snapshot, answer gate; next ordinary critique within the cap; auxiliary one-shot markers stay used. Closing leaves a question: bind a question generation and retain panes; the answer gate; the planner applies the answer before the critic. Current final hash approved with auxiliary passes already complete: commit final state and cleanup intents; approved result, with a cleanup warning if necessary. Any changed final spec requires a later ordinary APPROVE for that exact hash. After the closing confirmation approval, do not start a second closing or second advisory pass. If a question or directive requires more work after the one-shot passes, the ordinary loop continues within the cap. A disabled closing pass means the advisory result is retained for the user but does not create another planner turn.
4. Guarded restoration (rejected at cap). If optional closing changes do not obtain confirmation before the cap, the engine may return to the saved approved artifact when ALL hold: the original approval's binding inputs, human directive set, prompt/role/settings identities and context identity still match; no pending question, answer, steering receipt or unconsumed HUMAN.md observation; every owned agent turn is settled (a working or uncertain process/pane blocks restoration); under the owner lock SPEC.md still matches the last accepted planner-result hash and file observation. Then: save the exact rejected bytes at `rounds/closing-rejected.spec.md` with the closing/confirmation receipts; commit a restoration intent binding the current hash, the approved snapshot hash, the unchanged input basis and the rejected snapshot; recheck the current file observation immediately before atomic replacement; save a restoration receipt before finalization. On interrupted restoration the two bound hashes and the durable transaction determine whether replacement is pending or done; never start a model turn. Finalize the original exact-hash approval with `closing_result = rejected_at_cap` and links to the retained rejected changes. The final result includes `rejected_review_evidence`: each closing-confirmation critique path/hash, the rejected spec hash it reviewed, its verdict, and round/receipt ID. The final human message links these critiques and says they reviewed the rejected changes, not the restored final artifact; their objections can remain useful and restoration does not claim they were resolved. No new critic turn is needed for bytes already approved under unchanged inputs. If an input/directive changed or a question remains, keep impasse and the saved approved bytes (restoring could discard a binding user decision). An external spec/config mutation instead yields its declared conflict or handover, with no replacement. Never describe rejected closing bytes as approved.
5. Approval meaning. Approval means no material objection remains under the current review contract, on the recorded final bytes. It is not premise validation, implementation approval, or proof that the planned tool works. State this in the final human message, the guide and the JSON approval basis. Do not write an approval badge into SPEC.md unless the brief requested that artifact format. The final receipt names exact approved bytes, inputs, verdict and auxiliary status.
6. Final-result schema and input-stability check before final commit: pending unconsumed input is reported; a write after the final input snapshot is not retroactively included.

Outputs: auxiliary-pass records, final-result schema, and an optional-notes regression fixture (an approval that contains only non-blocking remarks and no trigger words), reduced to non-private representative content.

Fixtures used: F-DIRECT (owned Claude/Codex stubs; both planner assignments; one-shot and persistent); F-FILES.

Required: one fresh advisory session; ordinary verdict unchanged. Closing reads both complete reviews and runs once without a keyword trigger. Captured notes retained. Covers C06, baseline.
- A-FINAL-02 (tier A, F-DIRECT): first approval in the last allowed ordinary round with closing enabled and advisory notes. Required: skip closing, save no_round_left, finalize the exact approved hash, exit 0. No planner closing turn and no new question from that pass. Covers C06, C07.
- A-FINAL-03 (tier A, F-DIRECT): eligible closing leaves the same bytes or changes bytes; interrupt before/after the approved snapshot and closing receipt. Required: the approved snapshot is durable before launch. Same bytes finalize; changed bytes require a later ordinary APPROVE. Receipt recovery cannot start a second closing. Covers C01, C06, C07.
- A-FINAL-04 (tier A, F-DIRECT): changed closing then confirm_closing REVISE/MISSING, later APPROVE or cap exhaustion; vary unchanged inputs, new directive/question, unsettled turn and external spec edit.
