title: T06 Prove process deadlines, argument boundaries, child settlement
description: Why: in Bash, a requested CLI timeout is silently ignored when `timeout`/`gtimeout` is not installed (C03), and a killed controller can leave child agents running with no honest record of them (C11). The Go engine needs one shared process runner that enforces monotonic deadlines itself, keeps argument boundaries exact, never lets a child read the controller's stdin, and settles (or honestly fails to settle) owned children. Every later adapter (direct Claude/Codex, Gashki subprocess calls) reuses it, so it is proven first on both target systems (macOS and Linux).
design:
Work: implement the shared process runner in the `process` package (vendor prompt semantics stay out). Requirements:
1. Argument vectors only: build arguments as slices; no shell expansion or joined command execution. Spaces and control characters in paths, model strings and effort strings must not alter argv boundaries. Invalid control characters or leading option syntax where a vendor parser would treat the value as another flag are refused.
2. Null stdin by default: a child can never consume controller answers. Keep stdout, stderr, final reply and exit facts in separate owned sinks (files). Use bounded pipe handling and bounded drain/close waits (a descendant that retains stdout must not hang the controller).
3. Deadlines: a positive `wait_timeout` is one total turn budget on a monotonic clock, covering launch through completion and output collection. A resume uses the remaining saved budget and never resets it silently. Zero means no tool-imposed deadline. No dependency on `timeout`/`gtimeout`.
4. Process groups (macOS and Linux): start owned direct children in a new process group. On deadline or cooperative cancellation, send TERM to the verified owned group; wait a fixed 5-second grace interval; then KILL remaining owned members. Reap the direct child and drain/close pipes with bounded waits. Record signal, exit status, deadline cause, and uncertain child settlement. Go's process context support alone does not stop descendants; test descendants that retain stdout and descendants that ignore TERM. Use golang.org/x/sys (v0.48.0) for OS metadata where needed.
5. Verified owner identity: never trust a saved PID or PGID without current start-identity evidence (guards against PID reuse). After controller SIGKILL the manifest may show an active direct turn while its process still runs; if reliable identity cannot be established, the outcome is uncertain (later mapped to TURN_UNCERTAIN) and requires inspection. Do not launch a replacement turn from a partial spec. A next-turn action is released only after settlement and a valid recorded completion or explicit abandonment. Never kill by PID alone.
6. Typed outcomes: interrupted, not-started, uncertain, deadline-expired, exited. Include injected start failures and parent death with a retained child.
7. Persist timing and settlement facts without dumping environment values.
8. Unsupported platforms: reject any non-macOS/Linux process-control platform before an agent call (UNSUPPORTED_PLATFORM / exit 3).

Outputs: a shared process runner and target-system fixtures (owned executable stubs).

Fixtures used: F-PROC (owned executable stubs on macOS and Linux; descendants can ignore TERM, retain pipes, and survive controller death).
acceptance_criteria:
Done when: a deadline is enforced without timeout/gtimeout; spaces and control characters do not alter argv boundaries; cancellation reaps known owned children; an unknown saved PID identity leads to handover (uncertain outcome).
- A-PROC-01 (tier A, F-PROC): positive turn budget with no `timeout`/`gtimeout` on PATH; a descendant ignores TERM and retains stdout. Required: monotonic deadline, TERM then 5s grace then KILL, owned-child reap and bounded output settlement on each target OS. Covers C03, C11.
- A-PROC-02 (tier A, F-PROC): paths/model/effort with spaces and control text; the child tries to read stdin. Required: captured argv has exact boundaries; invalid control/option syntax is refused; stdin is null and cannot consume answers. Covers C03, C13.
- A-PROC-03 (tier A, F-PROC): runner harness with failed start, SIGINT/SIGTERM, parent SIGKILL with child alive, and reused PID observations. Required: typed interrupted/not-started/uncertain outcomes and verified settlement policy; no kill by PID alone. This is not a public checkpoint/exit proof (native owner exits are proved later by the review-engine and conformance tasks). Covers C01, C03, C11.
- Evidence rules for every case: report ID, tier, fixture, stimulus variant, source/binary hashes, settings, target OS (both macOS and Linux), observed output, process counts. A plan, a source comment, or a stub that merely returns the required answer is not evidence.
notes: A-PROC-01, A-PROC-02, and A-PROC-03 passed on macOS arm64 and Linux arm64 with owned executable stubs. The runner proves monotonic remaining budgets, TERM then five-second grace and KILL, bounded drain, exact argv, null stdin, typed outcomes, verified kernel start identity, and no signal from a partial or changed saved identity. Controller death retained one test child; verified fixture cleanup left zero live group members. Full macOS tests, process race tests, Linux process tests, vet, and diff checks passed. Public review recovery remains in later tasks.

title: T07 Build checkpoint transactions, receipts, locks, audit projection
description: Why: the Bash engine infers round and recovery state from file counts and modification times (C01), so a crash can lose work or repeat a prompt. The Go engine instead keeps one authoritative committed checkpoint (`state/manifest.json`) updated by small immutable transactions, so every external action has a durable intent before it happens and every advancement has a validated receipt. This task builds the whole storage layer, plus the protected-set comparator that later detects planner/critic tampering (C15), and defines recovery for every interrupted step before any external action is integrated. Interruption becomes testable without a model.
design:
Work (package `store`; must not own agent choice or model behavior):

A. Workspace file layout (owned and human-visible):
```text
WORKSPACE/
  BRIEF.md  CONSTRAINTS.md  SPEC.md  HUMAN.md  QUESTIONS.md
  volley.config.toml  gashki.config.toml
  rounds/  r00.response.md  rNN.critique.md  rNN.critique-retry.md  rNN.response.md
           rNN.answer-response.md  rNN.spec.md  rNN.human.md  rNN.questions.md
           second-opinion.md  closing-response.md  closing-approved.spec.md  closing-rejected.spec.md
  state/   manifest.json  owner.lock  control/  transactions/  turns/  prompts/
           inputs/ (inbox.jsonl)  logs/  events.jsonl  IMPASSE.md
```
BRIEF.md and CONSTRAINTS.md are optional inputs; at least a brief or a non-empty spec is required. Human files are user-facing channels, not the authoritative journal. Round names use at least two decimal digits and support the 9999 cap. A retry critique has its own immutable file; the accepted critique has a stable canonical path. The manifest links every accepted artifact to its content hash and turn receipt.

Reserved rounds basenames (whole-basename match; dots literal; `[0-9]+` is one or more digits): `r[0-9]+.critique.md`, `r[0-9]+.critique-retry.md`, `r[0-9]+.response.md`, `r[0-9]+.answer-response.md`, `r[0-9]+.spec.md`, `r[0-9]+.human.md`, `r[0-9]+.questions.md`, `second-opinion.md`, and `closing-*` (every extension). A planner may add new history such as `rNN.revision.md` but may not create a reserved name, even before its first commit (PLANNER_MUTATION, exit 8). New unreserved history becomes protected once committed. Before the controller creates a reserved artifact, an unexpected existing file is OUTPUT_CONFLICT; never overwrite it or treat it as review evidence. The executor may register one exact reserved critique path as the active Gashki critic output sink after proving it absent or a matching owned staged output; that grants the critic its current output only.

B. Manifest: one closed, versioned JSON schema. Field groups: `record_version`, `run_id`, `tool_version`, `source_commit`, `revision`, `last_transaction_id`; supplied workspace path, canonical physical path, device/inode ownership key, creation facts; run request key and canonical request hash; `status`, `phase`, current round, completed critic rounds, cap, control amendments; original setting sources, frozen config paths/hashes, prompt hashes, active executable bindings; planner/critic provider assignment and backend capabilities; vendor session records, Gashki pane records, server identity, per-turn cursor bindings; current turn ID, purpose, attempt, intent hash, delivery state, receipt path, artifact commit state; current spec hash, reviewed spec hash, verdict source, final approval basis; pending question generation, exact question bytes/hash, answer receipt IDs, application state; pending steering receipts and scheduled boundary; second-opinion and closing-pass states (one-shot completion markers, approved/rejected snapshot hashes, restoration intent/receipt, unchanged approval input basis); retention decisions, cleanup actions, unresolved errors, recommended next commands; last projected event sequence and derived-index registration status. Never store credentials, auth-file bytes, environment dumps or private Gashki ledger contents. Persist configured model/effort separately from observed model/effort; persist vendor session UUID, Gashki pane UUID, tmux target and turn cursor in different fields; nullable identity fields need an explicit evidence reason.

C. Transactions and crash recovery. `manifest.json` is the one authoritative committed snapshot. A transaction is a small immutable record: previous revision/hash, next full snapshot, staged artifact references, intended file operations. Write and fsync the transaction before replacing the manifest. Write the new manifest to a same-directory temp file, fsync, rename, sync the directory where supported. Only after this commit may the owner perform the external action named by its intent. After an external action, save a validated immutable receipt (never overwriting a prior receipt under the same turn ID) before committing the result transition. Recovery under the owner lock:
1. Validate the manifest, revision and every referenced record.
2. Examine any transaction immediately after the committed revision.
3. An uncommitted intent transaction proves preparation only, not delivery.
4. Roll it forward only if its previous hash and complete staged files match and no action was allowed before its commit.
5. A durable external receipt can complete the result transition after schema and bindings pass.
6. An intent committed without a trustworthy external result is unfinished or uncertain.
7. Use backend recovery rules; never infer completion from a non-empty artifact.
8. Project committed transitions into the event ledger by transaction ID and monotonically increasing sequence.
9. Ignore an incomplete final event line; a malformed committed interior record is a state error.
10. Repair a missing projection from committed transaction records without requesting an agent turn.
Events are a durable audit view, not an execution authority. A projection failure sets `audit_pending`; completion cannot claim all evidence complete while it is unresolved. The event reader exposes only committed records. Index registration is a separate best-effort projection and may warn without making the workspace unusable. A result commit may involve several files, but the manifest references only fully staged, verified artifacts; never mark a snapshot committed before its bytes and hash are durable. If an agent wrote a partial SPEC.md before a crash, preserve it as evidence; do not restore an old spec over it without an explicit recorded recovery decision.

D. Ownership and storage safety. Owned state directories mode 0700, owned records mode 0600 where supported; human-readable outputs follow caller umask unless a record carries sensitive local metadata. Refuse symlinks in owned state/control/transaction paths. Locks bind to the canonical physical workspace; confirm identity before writes. One controller lock is held while execution or answer-wait ownership is active. Human commands use a separate short inbox lock and can submit while an owner is waiting; saving an answer receipt does not need the controller lock. Under the inbox lock: save and sync an immutable input receipt, then append and sync its commit to `state/inputs/inbox.jsonl` before acknowledgment. Each journal entry has: schema version, consecutive sequence, previous-entry hash, run ID, input kind, key, generation ID (null for kinds that do not answer a question), receipt path, exact receipt hash. The journal records submissions only; the manifest still controls selection and application. Readers hold the inbox lock while validating the committed prefix and receipts. An incomplete final journal entry is not a commit; before another append recovery removes only that incomplete suffix under the lock. A malformed complete entry, broken sequence or bad receipt hash is STATE_INVALID; never discard a committed prefix to repair it. A receipt without a journal commit is pending evidence and cannot release a gate. An identical keyed retry may finish its journal commit after validation; a conflicting retry is refused. No acknowledgment before both records are durable; recovery syncs any validated complete prefix before returning a recovered acknowledgment. The OS releases ownership when the controller dies, which does not prove the agent stopped; an unfinished direct process or live pane can still block a new owner action. Never delete a lock file to bypass a lock. Bounded lock acquisition returns LOCKED with a safe wait/inspect recommendation.

E. Protected-set inventory, authorized-change registry and comparator (the store owns these; the review-engine task will wrap them around real turns). Protected set for every planner/critic turn: `state/**`, both frozen config records when present, BRIEF.md, CONSTRAINTS.md, and every existing committed `rounds` artifact. Record content hashes, file type, canonical path and device/inode observations; include `owner.lock` identity even if empty. Inventory protected directories so unexpected deletion, replacement, symlink or new state file is detected. The expected inventory lives in the owner's validated snapshot before the external action; never accept an agent-written manifest as expected state. The controller may update its own transactions, outputs, logs and event projection during a turn: track those exact authorized changes; validate separately registered output sinks and `state/control/` receipts; none grants the planner permission to edit `state/**`. Never exempt a whole state directory because a controller output inside it is active. For concurrent inbox submissions, save the validated journal head in the pre-turn inventory; afterwards under the inbox lock require the head unchanged-or-validly-extended, validate each appended entry and its receipt, and treat only exact journal-committed receipt files and the validated journal append as authorized inbox changes. An unreferenced new file or changed prior receipt is a protected-file change. New entries may record stale or losing candidates but cannot release a gate unless generation and selection checks pass. Pending receipt writes and incomplete journal suffixes are settled under the inbox lock before the comparator accepts a turn; an unresolved interrupted submission requires handover with retained evidence. (The comparator cannot authenticate the writer of a coherent forged receipt/journal pair under the Codex workspace-write boundary; document this limit.) After every completed or failed turn, compare the protected set to the expected inventory plus authorized changes, before trusting a receipt or starting another action. A planner change yields PLANNER_MUTATION (exit 8) with actor, paths, before/after observations and retained evidence; a critic change yields CRITIC_MUTATION (exit 8); an external/unknown writer yields ARTIFACT_CHANGED with actor=external_or_unknown. If checkpoint paths are no longer trustworthy, stop without adopting or repairing from changed records. Planner writable set: SPEC.md, QUESTIONS.md, and new review-history files under `rounds` that the turn request names or permits; reserved names are excluded even when absent; the comparator checks newly created rounds files for this rule; HUMAN.md is writable by the planner only during a user-started answer turn (which protects SPEC.md and QUESTIONS.md and permits only the answer append). Direct final-message/print outputs written by the vendor or controller are registered sinks.

F. Artifact limits: inputs/outputs must be regular valid UTF-8 files, no symlinks in owned output paths; 32 MiB per brief/spec/critique/output text file; promotion of outputs and snapshots happens in transactions; if completion is recovered after the receipt but before the snapshot, use the durable receipt and saved accepted spec hash to finish the snapshot without calling the planner again; keep partial failed artifacts under their turn directory.

Outputs: store package, state validators, protected inventory/comparator, authorized-change types, fault sites, deterministic recovery tests. Keep registry/index writes separate from execution authority. Unit cases use synthetic file changes and registered sink/control deltas, without a planner process or review loop.

Fixtures used: F-FILES (owned temporary workspace plus text/JSON files with exact bytes, inode/hash observations, symlinks, concurrent-writer controls).
acceptance_criteria:
Done when: intent is committed before any external action; valid receipts can finish a lost result commit; partial files cannot advance state; event projection repair causes no agent call.
- A-STATE-01 (tier A, F-FILES): interrupt before/after transaction fsync, manifest rename, directory sync and external receipt save. Required: no action before committed intent; only complete matching transactions/receipts advance; partial files cannot prove completion. Covers C01, C11.
- A-STATE-02 (tier A, F-FILES): the store harness supplies synthetic validated result/final snapshots and interrupts transaction, artifact promotion, revision snapshot and final commit. Required: store recovery is idempotent and binds the supplied receipt/hashes without an agent call; partial bytes stay retained. Approval-policy validation is proved later in the loop/final-approval tasks, not here. Covers C01, C07, C11.
- A-STATE-03 (tier A, F-FILES): missing event projection, incomplete trailing event, malformed interior event, failed index write. Required: rebuild the committed audit by transaction ID with no agent calls; interior corruption fails; audit_pending prevents a complete-evidence claim; an index warning leaves the workspace usable. Covers C01, C13.
- A-STATE-04 (tier A, F-FILES): lock harness with two owner processes via path aliases, symlink state, owner death with synthetic active-agent evidence, and concurrent inbox receipt writes. Required: one canonical owner; the short inbox lock permits receipt writes; owned symlinks are refused; lock release leaves supplied active-agent evidence unsettled (real process settlement is proved by process and loop tasks). Covers C01, C11, D03.
- A-STATE-05 (tier A, F-FILES): comparator unit harness simulates planner changes to manifest/lock/transaction/config/prior critique, undeclared state files, and creation of each reserved rounds name. Compare registered log/output/state-control deltas, concurrent committed inbox entries, unreferenced receipts, changed journal prefixes and new unreserved history. Required: the comparator returns a planner-mutation observation with actor/path evidence for each forbidden change and no false positive for exact authorized deltas. It does not run a planner or emit a public exit (end-to-end PLANNER_MUTATION / 8 is proved later). Covers C01, C11, C12, C15.
- Evidence rules for every case: report ID, tier, fixture, stimulus variant, source/binary hashes, settings, target OS, observed output, artifact hashes. A plan, a source comment, or a stub that merely returns the required answer is not evidence. Crash coverage includes every fsync/rename boundary.
notes: Implemented durable checkpoint transactions and receipt bindings, descriptor-relative no-follow storage, private directories, canonical owner and separate input locks, immutable input receipts with consecutive hash-bound journal commits, event projection repair with audit_pending and complete-evidence checks, exact protected inventories and authorized deltas. A-STATE-01 through 05 passed on macOS arm64 and Linux arm64, including abrupt test-process death and recovery interruption at sync/rename boundaries. Full Go suite, race checks, vet, contract and diff checks passed. No model calls occurred. Partial evidence is retained; active intent is not proof of delivery or completion. Mutable SPEC uses independent replacement files. Engine approval, backend settlement and public mutation exits remain in their own tasks. Proof: internal/store/STORE-PROOF.md.
close_reason: Implemented checkpoint transactions, receipt recovery, canonical ownership and inbox commits, audit projection, and protected-file comparison in ee04bb1. A-STATE-01 through 05 passed on macOS and Linux with process-death and recovery-boundary tests; full Go suite, race, vet, contract and diff checks passed. Storage policy limits are recorded in STORE-PROOF.md.

title: T08 Implement typed settings and config inspection/editing
description: Why: the Bash engine configures itself through scattered environment variables with no single record of what was in effect (C12). The Go engine replaces them with one flat TOML settings file plus flags, a closed typed setting table, recorded provenance for every effective value, and safe inspection/editing commands. This task builds the resolver and the config command handlers on top of the proven TOML/strict-JSON adapters and the shared process runner (executable resolution). Config commands must never start Gashki or a vendor tool.
design:
Work: implement declared-order typed settings, source locations, relative-path rules, active/inactive settings, schema, and `config` commands (`show`, `get`, `schema`, `validate`, `set`, `patch`, `edit`). Preserve comments through range edits. Centralize retired-variable warnings in doctor and capability declarations (the doctor command itself is rendered later by the inspection task; here supply the warning factory).

1. Selection and sources. `--config=PATH` selects the Volley file. Without it read `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/volley/config.toml`, otherwise `~/.config/volley/config.toml`. An empty XDG variable uses the home fallback. A non-empty relative XDG root is invalid for mutating commands. A missing default file means defaults. A missing named file fails, except for `config set`, `patch` and `edit` creation. `config validate PATH` requires the path to exist. An empty file is valid. Limit 1 MiB, valid UTF-8, regular input. Use one flat direct key per setting; reject unknown keys, tables, dotted keys, quoted key spellings, duplicates and reserved profile tables (the adapter from the TOML proof task supplies the grammar and line mapping; never regex-parse TOML). Validate the complete file before applying flags; an override cannot hide a bad file value.
2. Provenance. For every effective setting record `source = flag | file | default`. File source: absolute path plus 1-based key line. Flag source: canonical flag name plus argument position. Default source: the declared default plus the resolution rule. After a saved record is read back, its present keys have source file; do not claim the original source comments are current provenance.
3. Setting table. Record and validation order is the order below. All path strings reject NUL and invalid UTF-8. An empty optional string means a declared unset value, not a missing key. Durations parse with `time.ParseDuration`; positive-only durations reject zero.

| Key | Type / default | Flag | Validation or meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| planner | string / claude | --planner | claude or codex; the other provider is critic |
| backend | string / cli | --backend | cli or gashki |
| max_rounds | integer / 8 | --max-rounds | 1 to 9999; counts ordinary critic rounds |
| wait_timeout | duration / 0s | --wait-timeout | non-negative; zero means unlimited agent-turn budget |
| poll_interval | duration / 2s | --poll-interval | 10ms to 1m; file/answer and observation polling |
| persistent | boolean / false | --persistent | direct CLI only; true with Gashki is invalid |
| closing_pass | boolean / true | --closing-pass | at most one closing planner pass after first approval; skipped when no confirmation round remains |
| second_opinion | boolean / false | --second-opinion | one advisory fresh-session review per run |
| rubric | string / empty | --rubric | empty, security, data, decision-memo, or plan-spec |
| context_dir | path / empty | --context-dir | readable directory outside the workspace; canonicalize containment |
| claude_bin | executable / claude | --claude-bin | direct backend binding; inactive on Gashki |
| codex_bin | executable / codex | --codex-bin | direct backend binding; inactive on Gashki |
| gashki_bin | executable / gashki | --gashki-bin | checked Gashki executable when backend is gashki |
| gashki_config | path / empty | --gashki-config | empty selects the Gashki default; a named path must exist |
| claude_model | string / empty | --claude-model | empty leaves the vendor default unknown; otherwise non-empty identifier |
| codex_model | string / empty | --codex-model | same rule for Codex |
| claude_effort | string / empty | --claude-effort | empty, low, medium, high, xhigh, or max |
| codex_effort | string / empty | --codex-effort | non-control identifier; the vendor model validates support |
| claude_permission_mode | string / dontAsk | --claude-permission-mode | only dontAsk in this build; no permission-bypass setting |
| claude_planner_tools | string array / Read,Write,Edit,Glob,Grep,Skill | --claude-planner-tools | one JSON array flag value; closed file/Skill tool set |
| claude_critic_tools | string array / Read,Glob,Grep,Skill | --claude-critic-tools | no Edit or command tools; Gashki adds the required output Write |
| trust_folder | boolean / false | --trust-folder | Gashki spawn folder-trust choice only |
| placement | string / auto | --placement | auto, normal, or here; here requires a valid caller pane |
| allow_api_key | boolean / false | --allow-api-key | explicit billing-guard override; never copied from the environment |

Do not add a configurable Codex sandbox that permits writes to the reference directory. Planner uses workspace-write; direct critic uses read-only. The Gashki Codex critic has a weaker write boundary, declared by the direct/Gashki backend tasks. Record inactive settings but never execute or resolve inactive binaries. Warn on inactive binary overrides in plan and doctor. Model and effort strings are passed as one argument value, never as a shell command; reject embedded control characters and leading option syntax where the vendor parser would treat a value as another flag. Do not invent a list of model names or claim every model supports every effort; unsupported vendor choices fail as an upstream turn with saved evidence.
4. Paths and executables. File-sourced relative paths resolve against the file's directory. Flag-sourced relative paths resolve against the invocation cwd. Workspace paths resolve against cwd and retain both supplied and canonical forms. Resolve context and ownership containment through existing symlink parents. A context equal to or inside the workspace is invalid. A read-only context may be a symlink to a readable directory. Owned state paths cannot be symlinks. An executable with no slash is a PATH lookup name; with a slash it is a path under the source-base rule. Resolve active executables once before execution and record absolute path, version output and file hash when readable. Refuse a changed active executable on resume (no rebind operation exists yet). Do not bypass Go's current-directory executable lookup refusal.
5. Inspection. `config show` human output is valid TOML with fixed header comments and per-key source comments; `--toml` selects the same raw bytes; `--json` returns typed `config`, `_provenance` and selected-file metadata. `config get KEY` returns one typed value and its source. `config schema` declares all keys, defaults, bounds, path rules, inactive conditions and `additionalProperties: false`. `config validate` does no dependency or authentication launch.
6. Editing. `config set KEY VALUE` parses by declared type: strings are literal argument strings; arrays use strict JSON; integers and booleans use canonical forms. `config patch --from-stdin` reads one strict JSON object (limit 1 MiB); reject null, duplicate keys, trailing data, unknown keys and wrong types. An empty patch creates an empty absent file and otherwise is a no-op. Validate the resulting complete document before replacement. Replace only changed values using the adapter's value ranges; append missing keys in declared order after the existing document; preserve unrelated comments, whitespace, key order, line endings and literal content; a same-value update is a no-op and does not rewrite comments. Use a short cooperative file lock and compare the original hash/inode before atomic rename. A non-cooperating edit detected by the comparison returns OUTPUT_CONFLICT and retains the candidate. Refuse a symlink target for config mutation; read-only inspection may resolve a symlink.
7. `config edit` requires a terminal and runs EDITOR as an argument vector against a temporary copy. Default to `vi` when EDITOR is empty or unset. ASCII whitespace separates arguments; quotes group text; backslash escapes outside single quotes. No variable expansion, globbing, substitution, piping or redirection. Reject unmatched quotes and a trailing backslash. Validate after editor exit before replacement. Retain an invalid candidate and return its path. Do not replace a target that changed while the editor was open.
8. Retired variables. Do not read these as Volley settings: VOLLEY_PLANNER, MAX_ROUNDS, CALL_TIMEOUT, CLAUDE_BIN, CODEX_BIN, GASHKI_BIN, VOLLEY_BACKEND, VOLLEY_PERSISTENT, VOLLEY_CLOSING_PASS, VOLLEY_SECOND_OPINION, VOLLEY_CONTEXT_DIR, VOLLEY_PROFILE, VOLLEY_POLL, VOLLEY_TRUST_FOLDER, VOLLEY_ALLOW_API_KEY, and all four provider model/effort variables. Doctor reads these names only to report ENV_SETTING_IGNORED with replacement flags. Names without the VOLLEY prefix are retired only as inputs to Volley, not as global definitions for other tools. Keep OS conventions, vendor identity roots, vendor billing indicators and Gashki hook wiring; declare every such read in capabilities with purpose and scope. A compiled-out `VOLLEY_TEST_FAULT` trigger may exist in a test build only; it is not a product setting and is absent from release declarations. Do not strip all vendor identity variables as a side effect of removing settings variables.

Outputs: config handlers, TOML records, strict patch/editor input, file locks, provenance schemas. Do not start Gashki or a vendor from `config validate`.

Fixtures used: F-FILES (owned temporary workspace plus exact-byte TOML/JSON/text files, inode/hash observations, symlinks, concurrent-writer controls).

title: T09 Freeze records, identity context, and billing checks
description: Why: a review run must be reproducible and must not silently change settings, binaries, vendor identity roots, or billing exposure mid-run. The Bash engine reads environment variables fresh on every call and has no record of what it launched (C12), and its billing guard can proceed when its source cannot be read (C14). The Go engine saves resolved settings records into the workspace before any dependent action, hash-checks them before every external call, records caller and server vendor-root context without ever copying credentials, and refuses unknown billing context unless the caller explicitly overrides. This task builds that preparation layer, the pre-call hash gate and the child-environment builder, all testable with recording callbacks and no concrete vendor adapter.
design:
Work: resolve active executables once; save Volley and selected Gashki records before dependent mutation; query Gashki `state_dir` through the selected config; record caller/server root presence and checked effective roots; refuse unknown billing context without explicit override; build the pre-call frozen-config hash gate.

1. Record placement and freezing. Before spawn or direct agent launch save `volley.config.toml` at the workspace root; for Gashki also save `gashki.config.toml` there. Generate both atomically and record their hashes in the manifest (use the store task's transactions). Refuse a different existing record in a new run and offer a fresh workspace. Never mutate an original caller-owned config file. The Volley record includes every declared setting with typed values and absolute resolved path values; an empty optional value is written explicitly; active binary settings use the resolved executable path; for Gashki, `gashki_config` names the saved record's absolute path, and all later Gashki calls use that frozen file.
2. Pre-call gate. Before every direct launch and every Gashki call (including observe, wait, config reads and kill), verify the frozen Volley record hash and, when present, the Gashki record hash. Expected hashes come from the validated committed checkpoint and the owner's retained snapshot, never from an agent-modified manifest. A mismatch blocks the call with ARTIFACT_CHANGED plus actor/evidence fields and never loads the changed file as replacement settings. During initial preparation, before records exist, use stable observations of the selected input configs and commit the records before dependent execution. Test the gate through a recording callback harness for each external-call kind (direct launch; Gashki config, spawn, send, wait, observe, status, kill); no concrete vendor adapter is needed in this task.
3. Round cap. An increased round cap is recorded separately as a run-control amendment. A fresh run from the saved file uses the original recorded cap unless explicitly overridden.
4. Gashki record. Obtain it with checked `config show --toml` output (plain `config show` output is not TOML in the inspected implementation). Check process status and parse the result before committing. Query `config get state_dir --json` through the same selected config; use `data.value`, not `GASHKI_STATE_DIR` or a recalculated home path. Verify the frozen record resolves to the same mechanism values. An unset Gashki tmux socket is omitted from its record as Gashki declares; that omission does not pin an actual server, so record the actual server socket identity independently before dependent pane reuse. A saved record pins tool settings, not source content, vendor credentials or model output.
5. Layer ownership. L0 owns HOME, vendor config roots, authentication, personal skill setup, external identity. L1 (Volley) owns roles, requested model/effort, permitted tools, permission mode, workspace, context, budgets. L2 (Gashki) owns pane state, hooks, selected socket mechanism, ready/wait settings, internal event storage.
6. Identity context. Save presence and value of `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` and `CODEX_HOME` as identity-context metadata, not TOML settings. Distinguish absent, present-empty and present-with-value. Never export an assumed default for an absent variable. Save both the caller context and any checked server-effective context needed for Gashki. An unresolved actual context stays null with a reason and is not replaced by the caller's assumed home. A resume with a changed identity context returns IDENTITY_CONFLICT before any agent action. Gashki's inspected spawn copies the two vendor root variables when present in its caller; when absent, the tmux environment can supply them. The preparation proof checks server-effective roots and HOME through read-only tmux environment metadata. If the tool cannot determine the execution root its billing guard needs, it refuses before spawn unless the explicit billing override is set. That refusal must not change or delete the user's roots. Never copy root file contents or credentials into records. A resume with a changed active binary binding (path, version, hash) or server binding is refused before any callback.
7. Billing guard. When `allow_api_key` is false, check present API-key indicators and effective vendor auth/settings roots before launch: Claude `apiKeyHelper` configuration and non-null Codex API-key indicators, without displaying values. An unreadable required guard source is an explicit safety failure (BILLING_REFUSED), not permission to proceed. Report only the indicator name, path and refusal reason. The override records a boolean and the fact of explicit caller selection, never a secret.
8. Child environment builder. Centralize nested-Claude marker handling in the process environment builder. For direct nested calls keep the narrow removal of `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, `CLAUDECODE` and `CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT` when the nested marker is present. Record names removed, never values. Do not alter an unset `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` to a default. For Gashki use its documented spawn behavior; do not duplicate its private environment strip code. A configured default model stays requested-default/observed-unknown until real evidence names it.

Outputs: preparation receipts, config-record hashes, identity fields, safe guard diagnostics, child environment builder. No credentials enter records.

Fixtures used: F-FILES (exact-byte files, hashes, symlinks); F-GK-CANNED (owned Gashki process stub with canned envelopes, call records, simulated pane/server bindings).
acceptance_criteria:
Done when: a settings-record failure prevents spawn; the external-call gate rejects a changed Volley/Gashki record before it invokes its callback; all later Gashki calls use the frozen file; absent roots remain absent; changed identity or binary bindings prevent resume.
- A-REC-01 (tier A, F-FILES/F-GK-CANNED): preparation harness fails each record write/hash check before recording launch/spawn callbacks. Required: zero dependent callbacks; original configs unchanged. Frozen paths and queried `data.value` state_dir bind subsequent callback requests, without concrete adapters. Covers U08, C12.
- A-REC-02 (tier A, F-FILES/F-GK-CANNED): preparation/attachment guard harness with roots absent/empty/present, differing tmux roots, unknown actual roots, and changed saved root/server/binary bindings. Required: typed presence/refusal/override/binding results with zero callback on conflict and no secret bytes. Actual run resume wiring is proved later by the review-engine and integration tasks. Covers C12, C14.
- A-REC-03 (tier A, F-FILES): API indicators/helper in custom roots, unreadable guard file, explicit override, nested-Claude env markers. Required: BILLING_REFUSED without override; report names/paths only. Narrow declared removal list; effective vendor roots are unchanged. Covers C14.
- A-REC-04 (tier A, F-FILES): hash-gate unit harness labels recording callbacks as direct launch or config/spawn/send/wait/observe/status/kill. Change each frozen record before invocation. Required: gate returns typed ARTIFACT_CHANGED with zero callback invocations, from trusted expected hashes. It needs no direct-adapter, Gashki-backend or loop code; the review-engine and integration tasks prove the emitted exit and actual subprocess suppression. Covers C01, C12, C14.
- Evidence rules for every case: report ID, tier, fixture, stimulus variant, source/binary hashes, settings, target OS, observed output, artifact hashes. A plan, a source comment, or a stub that merely returns the required answer is not evidence.
notes: Implemented preparation receipts, private frozen settings transactions, stable original-input and active executable bindings, checked Gashki TOML/data.value mechanism queries, and retained hash gates for all external-call kinds. Caller/server identity metadata preserves absent, empty, present, and unknown values with reasons; server path/inode and executable path/version/hash changes block resume. Billing diagnostics retain only indicator names, paths and fixed reasons; explicit overrides and narrow removed environment names are recorded without credential values. A-REC-01 through 04 passed on macOS and Linux, including actual owned metadata subprocesses, record faults, lookup counts, cap replay, permission checks, and credential non-retention. Full Go suite, race, vet, contract and diff checks passed. Committed history is now checked before further store transactions. Proof: internal/agent/PREPARATION-PROOF.md. No vendor conversation occurred. Real pane/socket settlement, concrete adapter wiring and live enforcement remain separate tasks.

description: One-page AGENTS.md at repo root: what volley is (adversarial plan/critique loop, file-state, verdict protocol), the load-bearing invariants an agent must not break (machine-readable VERDICT last line; files are the only state; critic read-only; billing guard; role pinning; no stall detection BY OWNER DECISION — do not re-add), pointers to prompts/ and the mock-testing pattern (role-aware mocks + matrix under both VOLLEY_PLANNER values), and the bead workflow (br/bv) for planned work. title: Build-stage prompts: implementer-init/revise, code-critic
description: Write prompts/implementer-init.md (implement SPEC.md exactly; run the spec's Testing Strategy; write state/test-results.txt with each command, exit code, and trimmed output; record deviations in BUILD-NOTES.md; never edit SPEC.md), prompts/implementer-revise.md (address each objection by ID; fix or rebut into BUILD-NOTES.md Decision Log; rerun tests; refresh test-results.txt), prompts/code-critic.md (read spec, code, test-results, BUILD-NOTES, and — when git trail exists — the diff since the previous critique; severity-tagged objections; missing/failing test-results.txt is an automatic BLOCKER; style is explicitly out of scope; same VERDICT final line). Keep role voice consistent with existing prompts.

title: Build stage: volley implements the approved spec
description:
BACKGROUND: volley currently ends at an approved SPEC.md. The same adversarial mechanism — planner acts, critic gates with machine-readable verdicts, files carry all state — applies unchanged to producing working code. This is the leap from planning tool to autonomous dev pipeline.

GOAL: 'volley-build' wrapper (and --stage build in volley.sh): the planner implements SPEC.md inside the workspace (src/ plus whatever the spec dictates), RUNS the spec's own Testing Strategy, and writes results (commands, exit codes, trimmed output) to state/test-results.txt plus BUILD-NOTES.md for any deviation from spec. The critic reviews the code and results READ-ONLY — it never executes anything — with a code rubric: defect = code contradicts the spec, fails its own recorded tests, or misses a required edge case; style is out of scope. Same VERDICT protocol, separate BUILD_MAX_ROUNDS (default 8), rounds in build-rounds/ so plan history is preserved.

KEY DESIGN DECISIONS (settled here to avoid relitigating): critic stays read-only and trusts the recorded test artifact BUT must treat a missing or failing test-results.txt as a BLOCKER, which keeps the planner honest without giving the critic execution rights. Planner permissions: claude gets Bash added to allowed tools ONLY in build stage (it must run tests); codex planner already executes under workspace-write. Stage is pinned in state alongside roles.

DEPENDENCIES (hard, reflected in bead deps): severity-tiers — code review without severity discipline will not converge, style nits are endless; git layer — per-round commits are the diff medium the code critic reviews ('review the diff since your last critique' keeps later rounds cheap and focused).

WHY CONFIDENT: every mechanism transfers; both agents demonstrably write and revise real artifacts in this harness (four live runs). Risk is convergence discipline on code, which is exactly what the two dependency epics supply.

title: Test-results contract enforcement
description: Orchestrator-side guard rails for the artifact the critic trusts: after each implementer call in build stage, verify state/test-results.txt exists and was modified during that call (mtime vs a marker); if not, inject a one-shot reminder invocation (mirrors the missing-verdict retry pattern) before handing to the critic; log the anomaly. Never parse test outcomes in the orchestrator — judging results is the critic's job (per epic design decision); the orchestrator only guarantees the artifact's existence/freshness. ACCEPTANCE: mock implementer that 'forgets' the artifact triggers exactly one reminder then proceeds.

title: Verify build stage: mock plumbing + live datestamp pipeline
description: Mocks: stage pinning, prompt-set selection, build-rounds/ separation, artifact-freshness reminder, regression: full existing plan-stage matrix must still pass untouched. LIVE e2e: datestamp brief through plan stage (should approve in ~1 round) then volley-build; assert the produced script exists, is executable, running ./datestamp emits ISO-8601 UTC and exits 0 (verify by executing it ourselves in the test harness — do not trust state/test-results.txt for this assertion), and that state/test-results.txt matches observed reality. Then one live build on a meatier brief if budget allows. PASS/FAIL logging throughout.

title: CI mode (GitHub Action)
description: Action wrapper: on PRs touching briefs/, run volley in the runner, upload workspace as artifact, post REPORT.md summary as a PR comment. Requires deliberate billing decision (runners have no consumer subscriptions => VOLLEY_ALLOW_API_KEY=1 with metered keys, documented loudly, or self-hosted runner with logins). Rationale: makes volley a team artifact rather than a laptop tool; the billing guard's override exists precisely for this consciously-chosen case.

title: Closing pass: planner addresses non-blocking remarks after APPROVE
description:
STATUS: APPROVED by owner. This bead replaces the deleted severity-tiers epic after owner review found it heavier than the observed problem.

OBSERVED BEHAVIOR IT AUTOMATES (owner ground truth from manual volleying): frontier critics already self-tag "non-blocking minor" remarks in their approving round, unprompted; the owner routinely asks the planner to respond to those non-blockers anyway before closing, siding sometimes with planner and sometimes with critic. No imposed taxonomy needed — the critic natural labeling is the input.

MECHANISM: when the critic verdict is APPROVE, do not exit immediately. Run ONE final planner invocation with prompts/closing-pass.md: "the critic approved but noted non-blocking remarks in rounds/rNN.critique.md; address each one in SPEC.md or consciously decline it with a Decision Log entry; change nothing else." Then exit 0. If the approving critique contains no non-blocking remarks, skip the pass (cheap grep for the critic remark labeling; if ambiguous, run the pass anyway — the planner declining vacuously is harmless). Config: VOLLEY_CLOSING_PASS=1 default, 0 disables.

ALSO: one sentence added to prompts/critic.md blessing the labeling convention the critic already uses ("you may note non-blocking remarks alongside an APPROVE; label them clearly") so the closing-pass input stays reliable.

SCOPE GUARDS: no severity definitions, no objection IDs, no orchestrator parsing of tiers, no Accepted Risks appendix — all explicitly rejected as heavier than the problem. The closing pass planner call does NOT trigger a re-review; critic approval stands.

TESTS: mocks — approve-with-remarks triggers exactly one extra planner call then exit 0; approve-clean skips it; VOLLEY_CLOSING_PASS=0 skips it; REVISE rounds unaffected; full existing matrix regression. Live: one run on a brief known to produce closing remarks; verify Decision Log entries for each remark. PASS/FAIL logging.

title: Dual-run comparison harness (local-model experiment bench)

title: Fresh-eyes ratification pass after APPROVE
description:
BACKGROUND: each critic call is context-fresh (stateless design) but always reads the Decision Log, which anchors it to the debate's framing. Approval after N rounds therefore risks convergence-by-attrition, and a spec can pass while only making sense to someone who watched the argument.

GOAL: after the incumbent critic's APPROVE, run exactly one ratification review: same critic agent, but its input is SPEC.md with the Decision Log and Accepted Risks sections STRIPPED, and a dedicated prompt (prompts/ratify.md): 'you have never seen this project; is this spec complete, self-contained, and buildable exactly as written?' Same VERDICT protocol. APPROVE => log 'ratified' and exit 0. REVISE => its critique becomes the next rounds/rNN.critique.md and the loop continues normally (counts against MAX_ROUNDS). Config: VOLLEY_RATIFY=1 default, 0 disables. Livelock guard: at most one ratification cycle per run — a second incumbent APPROVE exits without re-ratifying (log states this).

WHY CONFIDENT: costs one extra agent call; directly tests the property users care about (spec stands alone); the stripped-log trick reuses every existing mechanism. This is the cheapest large trust win available.

title: Let review agents resolve technical design objections
description:

title: Git-native workspace audit trail + REPORT.md generator
description:
BACKGROUND: workspace history is cp snapshots (rounds/rNN.spec.md) plus logs. No diffs between rounds, no provenance, no single artifact a human can read end-to-end. The debate IS the product for a human reviewer, and today it is scattered across five files.

GOAL: (a) auto 'git init' inside the workspace (guard: skip if workspace is already inside a git repo, to avoid nested-repo surprises; then fall back to cp snapshots); one commit per event — initial draft, each critique, each revision — with structured messages like 'r02 revise: fixed r02-1, rebutted r02-2', author identity 'volley planner/critic <volley@local>'; tag final commit 'approved' or 'impasse'. (b) generate REPORT.md at exit: brief, outcome, per-round sections (critique text, spec diffstat, key Decision Log entries), Accepted Risks, timings from volley.log. Pure shell + git log/diff; zero new dependencies.

WHY CONFIDENT: git gives diffing/bisect/provenance for free and replaces hand-rolled snapshotting; every consumer of volley output so far (this project's own sessions) had to reconstruct the debate manually from rounds/*.

DESIGN NOTES: keep rounds/*.critique.md files (they are the critic-output capture medium); rounds/*.spec.md cp snapshots retained in v1 for grep-ability, marked deprecated in README once git trail is proven. title: Severity-tiered structured critiques (BLOCKER/MAJOR/MINOR)
description:
BACKGROUND: volley converges when the critic emits VERDICT: APPROVE. Today an objection is an unstructured numbered list item, and only rubric prose restrains nitpicking. The core failure mode of LLM critics is inflating minor preferences into round-burning objections; we currently fight it rhetorically, not structurally.

GOAL: every objection carries a severity tag and a stable ID: 'N. [BLOCKER|MAJOR|MINOR] (rNN-K) title' + body. Verdict rule becomes structural: REVISE if and only if at least one BLOCKER or MAJOR remains. MINORs are recorded into a '## Accepted Risks' appendix of SPEC.md instead of forcing revision rounds. Decision Log entries reference objection IDs, enabling later tooling (re-litigation detection, cross-round diffing) without committing to it now.

SEVERITY DEFINITIONS (to be embedded in prompts): BLOCKER = spec is wrong or unbuildable as written; MAJOR = a BRIEF.md requirement unmet or an internal contradiction; MINOR = an improvement that does not threaten correctness or feasibility.

WHY CONFIDENT: observed in live runs (job-queue brief, 3 rounds; swapped run, 2 rounds) that objection quality varies and rubric prose is the only brake. Tiering shortens volleys, makes every remaining round substantive, and produces an Accepted Risks record humans actually want.

SCOPE: prompts + orchestrator logging only; verdict grep protocol unchanged. No stall detection (explicitly excluded by project owner).

title: Tournament mode: both directions in parallel + synthesis
description:
BACKGROUND: planner direction is configurable and live runs exposed asymmetry — Claude-as-critic produced materially deeper critiques (3 detailed objections w/ failure scenarios) than Codex-as-critic (1/round); each planner also drafts differently. For high-stakes briefs, one direction leaves value on the table.

GOAL: volley-tournament <workspace>: run cc-volley and codex-volley concurrently in sub-workspaces A/ (claude plans) and B/ (codex plans) from the same BRIEF.md. When both converge: cross-review — each agent critiques the OTHER side approved spec once (severity-tagged); then a synthesis invocation (default planner: claude, configurable) merges both specs + both cross-reviews into SPEC-FINAL.md, choosing the stronger treatment per topic and recording every choice in a "## Synthesis Log".

FAILURE HANDLING: one side impasses => proceed with the survivor (skip cross-review of the dead branch, note it in Synthesis Log); both impasse => tournament impasse, both IMPASSE.md files surfaced.

COST: ~2x a single volley plus 3 calls — acceptable by owner stated indifference to plan-quota usage; document in README regardless.

STATUS: idea approved for further consideration by owner (not yet greenlit for implementation).
